name: Fix optical magnification source resolution
description:
## Goal
Fix Critic R2: refractive-lens and focal Magnify soften text because they enlarge native-resolution source textures with linear filtering.

## Evidence
- Critic recommendation: IMPLEMENTATION-FIX-REQUIRED
- Refractive lens: p0.25 at (1510,260), normalized edge step 0.8396 vs native 0.9866
- Focal Magnify: p0.15 at (2150,620), normalized edge step 0.8389 vs native 0.9978
- Responsible paths: src/lib/pipelines/effects/refractive-lens/index.ts and src/lib/pipelines/surfaces/paper/pipeline.ts

## Requirements
- Fix source resolution in the rendering pipeline; do not reduce authored magnification in Preset JSON.
- Preserve native 3840x2160 / 2160x3840 output, premultiplied alpha, frame determinism, preview/export parity, and outside-region pixel identity.
- Apply one coherent resolution strategy to the composition Effect and focal Annotation paths.

## Done when
- Focused tests and static gates pass.
- Native flagged-Chrome captures have no WGSL/runtime errors.
- R2 probe no longer reports softened transformed text.
- Fresh isolated Critic returns ACCEPT with zero pipeline-bug/default-too-permissive findings.
result: Replaced linear optical enlargement with shared sharp cubic reconstruction in refractive-lens and Magnify. Final Critic measured transformed text equal to native sharpness in both orientations; focused tests, check, preset verification, build, and native captures pass.

name: Mix clip audio and classify coverage
description:
## What
Decode each enabled clip source interval into its exact destination sample range, mix with Supers cues/bed deterministically, and make opacity/output classification depend on full timeline coverage rather than media presence.

## Why
Hard cuts, trims, multiple clips, gaps, gain, and transparent output must remain synchronized across preview/export without painting black.

## How
Share clip interval/source mapping with visual resolution; decode/mix clips at 48 kHz with collision-free ordered intervals, clip gain/enabled controls, and deterministic cancellation. Classify opaque only when explicit fill/stage or Video clips cover the required composition interval; unused assets and gaps must not imply opacity. Adapt sanitized Sentry context without media IDs/names/URLs.

## Done when
Focused audio decoder/mix/preview/export/output-classification tests prove sample placement, cut boundaries, gaps, gain/disable, cues/bed combination, and codec plan selection.

## Backend implementation context — 2026-07-28
- Added shared half-open Video clip Timeline/Source intervals and full-transport union coverage. Visual frame resolution, audio placement, opacity, bed eligibility, and diagnostics now use the canonical semantics.
- Audio decodes enabled, nonzero-gain clips sequentially at 48 kHz into absolute frame-derived sample ranges; gaps/disabled clips stay silent, gains apply before deterministic cue/bed summing and the single peak ceiling. Full-span migrated clips reuse decoder PCM to preserve prior behavior and bounded memory.
- Preview chooses the exact offline mix when clip audio participates; pause/loop cancellation remains wired.
- WebM uses opaque naming/codec only for full clip coverage or explicit fill/stage; gapped tracks and unused Media remain alpha overlays. ProRes remains 4444.
- Replaced singular Source-video Sentry context with scalar aggregate Media/Video-track context containing no IDs, names, URLs, bytes, codec/probe data, or creator content.
- Canonical EngineState and Preset application no longer synthesize or consume sourceVideo; legacy ingress migration remains. Concurrent Media authoring must remove remaining Svelte-only sourceVideo reads before project-wide typecheck.
- Targeted verification: 9 files / 56 tests passed; focused Prettier and ESLint passed; no TypeScript any added. No docs, automation, commits, or task status changes.
result: Implemented exact clip-interval 48 kHz audio decode/placement/mix with gain/disable, gaps, cuts, cues/bed and cancellation; added full-coverage Video-track opacity/bed eligibility and privacy-safe aggregate export telemetry; removed backend runtime sourceVideo synthesis/use. Focused audio/preview/export/classification/schema suites: 9 files, 56 tests passed plus 18 Sentry/export and 6 audio-mix tests; targeted Prettier/ESLint/diff check passed. No commit.

name: Healthy engineering delivery gates
description:
## Goal
Make local and automated delivery checks trustworthy for the local creator app and browser renderer.

## Requirements
- Keep TypeScript pinned to 6.0.3 until svelte-check and typescript-eslint support TypeScript 7.
- Configure svelte-check and ESLint to inspect source files rather than generated build output.
- Clear genuine source type and ESLint failures.
- Add one SvelteKit-aware test runner and package test scripts.
- Browser integration and render-pixel tests must launch or connect to Chrome with --enable-blink-features=CanvasDrawElement; assert copyElementImageToTexture exists before testing and fail fast when the flag is absent. Reuse the CDP 9223 / scripts/cdp-capture.mjs contract locally and make CI provision the same flagged browser rather than using generic Chromium.
- Add required CI for frozen install, check, lint, tests, verify-presets, browser integration, and build.
- Add persistence API and export integration coverage for the local app.

## Done when
- Every named command is green from a clean install.
- CI runs the same commands, including a flag-enabled HTML-in-Canvas browser test.
- Browser tests prove the CanvasDrawElement feature is present before making render assertions.
- Local export and persistence behavior is tested.
result: All delivery gates green and committed (9aa006d). check: 921 files/0 errors; lint: clean (eslint scoped to source, docs-site + generated d.ts ignored); test: vitest 11 files/16 tests incl. new export + user-compositions API coverage; test:structural: 3 scripts; verify-presets: 35 fixtures; build: clean; test:browser: proves copyElementImageToTexture flag, native 3840x2160, non-uniform render via cdp-capture/9223 contract. Quality CI workflow mirrors the exact command set with frozen install + flag-enabled Chrome (clean-install proof lands on first push). TS pinned 6.0.3.

name: Fix undefined --surface-1 — the rail panel background never renders (F-03)
description:
## What
Inspector.svelte:109 sets background: var(--surface-1) but the variable is undefined (measured '') — the declaration silently resolves to transparent and the rail sits on body #050505, itself off-ladder (neither ink #0C0C0E nor deck #131315).

## Why
The three-zone architecture (canvas / rail / timeline as distinct surfaces) is invisible; only the 1px border separates the inspector from the canvas surround. A dead var is also a latent trap for every future surface.

## How
Rail → background #131315 (deck); canvas surround → #0C0C0E (recessed). Delete the dead var or define it at the workspace root — decide once, one convention.
Evidence: getComputedStyle(aside).getPropertyValue('--surface-1') === ''; computed backgroundColor rgba(0,0,0,0); body rgb(5,5,5).

## Done when
The rail renders an opaque spec-ladder panel background and no CSS in the workspace references an undefined custom property.
result: Chrome neutral ladder (--chrome-text/muted/deck/well/raised/hairline) defined once at the Workspace root; rail renders opaque deck #131315 (measured rgb(19,19,21)), canvas surround recessed #0C0C0E; --surface-1 deleted (Inspector uses --chrome-deck, VideoFrame fallback uses --chrome-well). getPropertyValue('--surface-1')==='' confirms no reference remains.

description: New domain (ADR-0033, AMENDED 2026-07-02). The sound rides the animation: motion primitives emit semantic sound events at their own frame, intrinsic to the motion. FINAL MODEL (post-epic by-ear rounds with Scott, commits 820ec5a..d9b438e): motion → event (motion-character rules; per-side chat events pop/send) → ONE engine-default sample (DEFAULT_EVENT_SAMPLES in sound-cues.ts) → per-motion override (sample lock / mute) from any inspector or the timeline's Sound rail. The §3 Sound-kit/palette concept was REMOVED after four GUI legibility failures; the ADR-0024 core fallback was removed with it (uncovered = silence). Fade/press/glide motions are silent by character. audioCues[] holds free-standing sounds + the bed ('Sound' section at root, added at the playhead). Determinism: offline JS fixed-order mix (byte-identical) muxed into WebM (opus) + ProRes (pcm); preview playback-only, scrub silent. Samples: CC0 desk-world recordings + Apple Messages sounds at Scott's direction (⚠ not redistributable). Epic closed 10/10; amendments documented in ADR-0033 + docs/preset-format.md + glossary.
result: Epic complete (10/10, 2026-07-01, commits 8524559..c1e18f1). Sound design shipped end-to-end per ADR-0033: schema (audioCues[]/per-Layer soundKit/per-motion overrides) → derived motion emission → kit registry+resolver with core fallback (7 deterministic synthesized core WAVs) → deterministic offline mix (JS fixed-order summing; byte-identical renders) → WebM opus + ProRes pcm muxing → playback-only preview (scrub silent) → escape-hatches fixture → timeline Sound rail → inspector Sound sections → first designed kit 'syntax' (CC0 quick fwips, by-ear approved by Scott) on the newspaper reference deliverables + lower-third + chapter-card (with ambient bed). name: Preset picker home screen — SVG-icon card grid (ADR-0034 §8)
description:
Prior task u0yxi2de marked complete but what shipped is NOTHING — flat text links with a subtitle, no design at all. It must look like a real screen in a real app.

TARGET (explicit from the user): a card GRID where each preset card has a representative SVG ICON for its surface/tool type — chat bubbles for iMessage, a browser/webpage window for web-document, a newspaper glyph for newspaper, a paper sheet for paper, etc. Nothing crazy — clean line SVGs — but enough that the card 'looks like something real in an app' instead of a text row. SVG icons avoid needing rendered preview thumbnails.

Two sections per §8: 'Starter templates' (corpus presets, read-only, fork-on-first-edit) and 'Your compositions' (user forks, each with a delete affordance). Cards: icon + name + surface label + compositor badge (2.5D/3D) where relevant. Match the dark recessive editor aesthetic (§7). NO table/row layout. Adequate visual hierarchy — name prominent, meta secondary.

Build a small surface-type → SVG icon map (in src/lib/utils per the utils rule, or a colocated icon component set). Apply design-engineering + ux-interface-design + typography + graffiti-best-practices.

DONE: grid of icon cards, one icon per surface type, two labeled sections, delete on user comps, dark aesthetic, no text-link list. Chrome screenshot proof of the home screen required before close.
result:
Replaced the home picker's SVG surface glyphs with real rendered composition posters.

Mechanism (HTML-in-Canvas only rasterizes top-level, so no background iframe):
- Capture-on-view: Workspace snapshots its settled frame via canvas.toBlob (createImageBitmap returns empty on WebGPU canvases) -> WebP stored under a content-hash key (src/lib/platform/posters.ts, api/posters/[key]/+server.ts, .posters/ gitignored). Self-healing: changed composition -> new key -> re-render on next view.
- Surface defaults: 9 committed static/surface-posters/*.webp are the instant cold fallback (cover every card immediately); a composition poster overrides per-card once it exists. Chain: composition -> surface -> glyph.
- Warm pass: scripts/warm-posters.mjs drives the flag-Chrome through all 58 compositions to pre-fill the cache; capture-surface-posters.mjs regenerates the 9 defaults.
- PosterCard.svelte: 16:9 stage, thumbnails bleed to card edges over a blurred cover-scaled backdrop (portraits fill without bars), uniform 256px card heights, hover lift+shadow. Renamed off Graffiti's .card primitive which was injecting 16px padding.

Verified (Chrome DevTools MCP, flag-Chrome localhost:7263): cold gallery /  -> all 60 cards show a real thumbnail from surface defaults (0 skeleton/glyph); viewing /p/web-document-twitter generated its poster and its card upgraded to the real Twitter render while siblings stayed on the Wikipedia default; warm pass filled 57/60 to their own composition poster; measured card padding=0 (gaps=1px border) and uniform heights=256px. svelte-check clean (only 2 pre-existing engine-schema baseline errors). Commit a233393.

name: probe-hue-count: downsample pre-pass for mask/subpixel Effects
description: Critic crt-tube-demo (2026-07-10): probe-hue-count counts phosphor-mask subpixels and NTSC chroma confetti as saturated palette hues (12 bins on p0.50) — Q4 cannot be machine-checked on subpixel-structure Effects. name: Schema: keyframes[] + per-property ease + cascade anchors
description:
ADR-0035 §5. engine-schema.ts:

name: Resizable timeline panel in landscape — ADR-0034 §7: timeline height fixed 220px in portrait; in landscape it shares vertical space with the canvas and must have a drag handle to resize. description: ADR-0034 §7 — timeline height is fixed 220px in portrait but drag-resizable in landscape (viewport wider than tall), where it shares vertical space with the canvas. Add a horizontal drag handle at the top edge of the .workspace__timeline panel; dragging it up/down changes the timeline height (the canvas 1fr row absorbs the change), clamped to a sensible min/max. Only active in landscape; portrait stays a fixed 220px and shows no handle. result:
Resizable timeline panel in landscape (ADR-0034 §7) + fixed a canvas-squish bug it surfaced.

FILES: Workspace.svelte (resize), VideoFrame.svelte (canvas fit).

RESIZE: timeline height is component state (default 220px). In landscape (viewport wider than tall) a 7px ns-resize drag handle sits at the top edge of .workspace__timeline; dragging it adjusts --timeline-h (grid row), the canvas 1fr row absorbing the change, clamped [140, viewportH-220]. The chosen landscape height persists in state across orientation flips. <svelte:window> binds innerWidth/innerHeight; onDestroy removes the drag listeners.

name: paper-grain invisible on near-black fields (additive option / lift dark bumpers)
description: From the text-3d Critic (2026-06-21, non-gating aesthetic-miss). paper-grain is MULTIPLICATIVE (out = rgb*(1±0.06*density)); on a near-black backgroundFill like #040408 (luma ~0.018) the per-frame shimmer is ~0.0002 luma = below visibility. So even after the effect-chain fix (grain now reaches the opaque backgroundFill), the grain reads as nothing on dark bumpers — verified background-only region 0 changed px on text-3d. The dark full-frame bumpers (text-3d, counter, instance-stack, cursor-trail, all on #040408) get NO living grain layer. Options: (a) add an ADDITIVE grain mode/term so grain is visible on near-black, or (b) lift the bumper fields slightly off pure-black (graded backdrop) so multiplicative grain + tone have something to live in. Pairs with the systemic 'flat CSS on black' audit deficit — these 4 bumpers have flat #040408 voids vs the graded backdrops the surfaces got. Low priority; the bumpers are Critic-ACCEPTed (foreground motion carries their holds).
result: Option (a) shipped: paper-grain gains a lift param (zod default 0 → byte-identical for every existing composition; x + 0·grain is bit-exact). lift couples the same two-octave grain field ADDITIVELY, weighted (alpha − luma) — full on opaque near-black, zero on bright content and transparent pixels (premultiplied-correct, E4 holds). Editor slider shipped with it (parity); pack() guards missing lift with ?? 0 for the raw-manifest pack-chrome lane. The three dark bumpers still authoring grain (counter-milestone, cursor-trail-title-sweep, instance-stack-vertical) author lift 0.3; text-3d no longer carries grain post-re-dress. Verified on counter-milestone 4K CDP captures: field liveness went 2% of px (dither-level, the dead field this task described) → 48% at max ±2/255; delta-by-luma monotone 0.37→0.09; amplified crops show organic structure that also masks field banding; frame at 1x still reads flat warm-black (Q12/brand-safe). name: Glow-form depth has no torn-silhouette synthesis lane
description: Known limitation shipped with 6ltfmkwx (noted in newspaper CanvasSource + crt manifest): the newspaper's edge is now intrinsically torn, so its CSS depth branch is dead and the pack's newspaper depth claim reaches pixels only through the edge-treatment ShaderPass's synthesized shadow — which handles hardOffset rigs only. crt-terminal's core glow depth therefore does not reach the clipping at all (no bloom rim on newspaper under crt; previously crt claimed edge 'none' and took the CSS glow branch). Fix: teach the edge pass (or a sibling pass) to synthesize a bloom halo from the torn silhouette alpha — a centered blur of the silhouette in the glow color, composited under the card. Low urgency: affects only glow-depth packs x torn-edge surfaces (today exactly crt-terminal x newspaper).
result: Edge pass gained the glow lane: EdgeTreatmentDepthRig union (offset|glow); glow synthesizes a two-ring bloom halo (8 taps at radius, 8 at 2.25x, intensity-weighted, CSS-era layering) around the torn silhouette, composited under the card. crt newspaper bloom restored — phosphor halo hugs the tear and shines through notches (native-4K verified). Depth 'fg' sentinel now resolves the PACK ink voice via resolvePackRoleColor (depth is claimable chrome; syntax byte-identical, crt gets phosphor not newsprint). Bonus fix: cssColorToRgbaFloat parses rgba() rig colours — clean-light's quiet float now carries its 0.1 alpha instead of collapsing to opaque black hard shadow.

name: Build exact Video clip edit model
description:
## What
Add typed Video track/clip identities, selection routing, timeline-row construction, and pure integer-frame move/trim/slip/drop/snap math.

## Why
A fixed one-track model with multiple non-overlapping clips cannot reuse normalized animation-ramp math or stringly Layer identities.

## How
Create concept-focused utilities in src/lib/utils, keep immutable drag origins, enforce frame-grid writes, source-duration bounds, composition bounds, neighbor collision clamps, half-open intervals, and deterministic tie breaking. Body moves start; left edge changes start/duration/source start by the same frame delta; right edge changes duration; Alt/Option interior changes only sourceStartSeconds.

## Done when
Focused identity/track/edit-math tests cover empty track, ordering, drops, edge cases, NTSC transport, collisions, source bounds, all gesture semantics, and no Video entry in Add layer.

- Added src/lib/utils/video-clip-edit.ts for immutable-origin move, left/right trim, slip, drop, integer snapping, source/composition/neighbor clamps, half-open gap insertion, exact rational NTSC conversion, and earlier-frame tie resolution. TimelineOutline, Media rail, decoder/audio, and Add layer UI were intentionally untouched.
- Targeted verification: 5 Vitest files passed, 34 tests; scoped ESLint passed; git diff whitespace check passed. A reviewer-run full svelte-check remains non-zero only because of 5 unrelated pre-existing/concurrent errors in achievement.test.ts, html-in-canvas.ts, and composition-frame-renderer.test.ts.
- Handoff for om4d7cdk: consume VideoTimelineTrack via isVideoTimelineTrack, capture createVideoClipDragOrigin once per pointer gesture, and call resolveVideoClipDrag/resolveVideoClipDrop on each update. Media/Video remains absent from Add layer.
result: Added typed Video track/clip identities and selection, fixed non-removable Video row, and pure immutable-origin integer-frame move/left-trim/right-trim/slip/drop/snap math with source/composition/neighbor clamps. Focused suite: 5 files, 34 tests passed; targeted ESLint/diff check and Svelte autofixer (0 issues/0 suggestions) passed. UI integration remains in om4d7cdk. No commit.

description:

ADR-0034 §9 specifies 'progressive disclosure via a plain chevron toggle on the section label, no expand/collapse animation' — nothing in the rail is collapsible. Block-inspector content measures 1141px in a 680px viewport; Keyframes/Cascade/Sound/Text Motion live below the fold on every selection.

## Why
The spec'd mechanism for managing rail depth is absent, and the rail already overflows on the most common selection.

## How
Chevron disclosure on section heads (snap at 0ms per the motion rule), default-open for content + position, collapsed state remembered per session. Alternatively amend ADR-0034 §9 to declare always-expanded intentional — one of the two, decided and landed (same shape as homepage F-08).

## Done when
Either sections disclose via plain chevrons with 0ms snap, or ADR-0034 §9 is amended — decided once.
result: Decided: implement ADR-0034 §9 as written (no amendment). InspectorSection discloses via a plain chevron trailing the label (label stays flush left preserving the shared grid), 0ms snap, aria-expanded button; open state remembered per session in a module-level map keyed by label. Keyframes/Cascade/Sound/Text Motion default collapsed via defaultOpen={false}; content/position/enter/exit default open — block-inspector content now fits common viewports and depth is disclosed, not scrolled.

name: Design critique: Homepage / preset picker — bring under DESIGN.md
description:
Epic from the 2026-07-09 /ui-design-critique of the homepage (preset picker, src/routes/+page.svelte + PosterCard.svelte). Full report in the critique conversation; DESIGN.md (repo root) is the binding spec.

VERDICT: Well-built, distinctive page — smoke test clean at all viewports (1440/1280/485/375), execution precision near-perfect (all left edges 34.5px, grid gaps 21.5px, identical metrics across 101 cards). The core problem is IDENTITY DRIFT: the page runs a local --race-* palette and uses the signal lights decoratively, which DESIGN.md (authored 2026-07-09, AFTER this page) now defines as violations. These are 'bring the page under the new spec' work, not craftsmanship failures. One confirmed accessibility failure: card meta labels at 3.76:1 contrast.

FINDINGS: 16 — P0: 0 · P1: 4 (F-01..F-04) · P2: 7 (F-05..F-11) · P3: 5 (F-12..F-16). One task per finding under this epic.

NOTE ON SEQUENCING: F-07 (spec neutral ladder) changes the background values that F-01's contrast target is computed against — land F-07 first or fix F-01 with the spec ladder values (muted #8A8A90 on #131315 passes at ~5.6:1). F-03/F-06/F-08/F-12 are one coordinated re-theme pass if convenient.

PRESERVE — DO NOT REGRESS (strengths from the report):
1. Execution precision: all left edges exactly 34.5px; 21.5px grid gaps; identical card metrics across 101 cards.
2. Spatial rhythm: heading→grid 24px < section gap 37.4px (outer > inner); zero boxes-in-boxes.
3. States engineering: poster fallback chain (composition → surface poster → glyph), shimmer skeletons, lazy loading, prefers-reduced-motion handling; empty 'Your compositions' unrenders.
4. Brand moment: Archivo Black Italic shout + checkered-flag glyph + hard-offset shadow — unmistakable POV, AI-slop risk Low.
5. Focus states: focus-visible yellow outlines already match the spec's selection grammar exactly.
6. Mobile reflow: clean single column at true 375px; delete affordances surface without hover on touch.
result: All 16 findings from the 2026-07-09 homepage critique landed in one coordinated pass (commit 8508419) and verified in Chrome at 1440 and 375 (touch-emulated). Identity drift resolved: spec neutral ladder in place (zero tinted neutrals), signal lights state-only, two type voices honest (Archivo structure / mono values), motion at spec (120ms border/bg only), radii+spacing on token, template wall grouped into 13 families (max run 14), fixtures collapsed, in-place two-step delete confirm, wordmark shadow + spec plate codified in DESIGN.md. Strengths preserved: left edges/grid gaps identical across cards, outer>inner rhythm, poster fallback chain + shimmer + reduced-motion intact, brand moment untouched, yellow focus grammar unchanged, clean 375px single column. Contrast failure fixed: meta labels 5.41:1.

name: Rubric: authored-signal-degradation clause for R1/R4/Q4
description: From the Critic reports for ntsc-signal-demo and crt-tube-demo (both ACCEPT, 2026-07-10): R1 (text sharpness), R4 (edge AA), and Q4 (hue cap) carry no authored-signal-degradation exemption, so any NTSC/CRT/VHS-class Effect fixture technically fails them as written even when the pipeline is correct — both Critics had to judge 'at fixture terms' manually. R2 already has the analogous permanently-defocused authored-softness exemption. Suggested rule: when a Preset declares a signal-degradation Effect, R1/R4/Q4 are judged as 'degradation matches the declared signal model' (raster pitch, bandwidth, subcarrier period verified numerically against params), not against the pristine bar. Where: docs/quality-rubric.md.
result: Updated docs/quality-rubric.md with a narrow authored signal-degradation scope for R1, R4, and Q4. Registered signal-model Effects such as ntsc-signal and crt-tube may now be judged against their declared bandwidth, raster, mask, and subcarrier behavior, but only with named parameters and measured output evidence; unrelated blur, aliasing, and palette noise still fail. Added the required R-protocol verdict syntax, Q4 viewing-distance downsample rule, and synchronized checklist/hard-rejection language. Verified with git diff --check.

name: Fix optical orientation defaults
description:
## Goal
Resolve the final Critic defaults blocking optical-lens-showcase ACCEPT.

## Findings
- Paper vertical body cap height is 41.51 px at src/lib/pipelines/surfaces/paper/CanvasSource.svelte, below the G4 44 px floor.
- Normalized optical regions scale independently by frame axis, changing the frosted pane from 307x518 px (aspect 0.59) horizontal to 173x922 px (aspect 0.19) vertical. Clear-lens geometry uses the same region contract.

## Requirements
Make Paper body sizing orientation-aware without regressing horizontal measure. Resolve optical regions through one shared aspect-preserving policy based on canonical 16:9 authored geometry, keeping regions in-frame and applying to both refractive-lens and frosted-glass. Preserve deterministic native rendering and alpha behavior.

## Done when
Horizontal/vertical captures show safe typography and intentionally preserved optical aspect; focused tests and all repository gates pass; fresh isolated Critic returns ACCEPT.
result: Resolved vertical Paper typography, aspect-preserving optical regions, T1 Paper presence/area, and practical platform-rail defaults. Final vertical Paper is 2008.8x3264 (79.05% area, 85% height), body cap 44.997 px, readable right edge x=1900.8.

name: instance-stack: per-item stagger driven by raw clock (BAD)
description: VerticalStackCanvasSource.svelte:12 / HorizontalTrainCanvasSource.svelte:12 set progress=animState.globalProgress, fed to motionShape which staggers each item: lag=(i/(count-1))*lagWindow, riseDuration=max(0.04,lagWindow*0.25), smoothstep(lag,lag+riseDuration,progress) (vertical-stack.ts:23-29, horizontal-train.ts:23-27). Stagger keyed to globalProgress=0, not the overlay enter; buildTracks shows only the single overlay enter/exit clip so per-instance pop-in is invisible/uneditable — same shape as iMessage. Mitigation: lagWindow IS schema; riseDuration 0.04/0.25 hardcoded. Fix: per-instance enter:{start,duration} anchored to the overlay enter window + per-instance sub-tracks in buildTracks (mirror Workspace.svelte:545-571); promote riseDuration to schema.
result: instance-stack stagger now schema+timeline. Added staggerStart schema field (default 0 = zero behavior change); variant CanvasSources anchor progress = globalProgress - staggerStart; buildTracks emits a draggable 'stack' clip (start=staggerStart, width=lagWindow) writing back to content. Verified vertical-stack preset renders identically + the clip shows.

name: Animation timing → schema + timeline (audit remediation)
description: Audit (2026-06) found surfaces/overlays that bake animation TIMING into components/shaderPasses with hardcoded constants driven by the raw globalProgress/ctx.progress clock — invisible to buildTracks + the GUI. Fix to the imessage pattern: per-element enter:{start,duration} schema descriptor + a draggable buildTracks clip (precedent Workspace.svelte:545-571), or drive shader entrance phases from the existing surface.enter track instead of magic progress constants.
result: All 7 audit-remediation subtasks complete — animation timing moved from baked-in component constants to schema descriptors that render as draggable timeline clips (buildTracks), so GUI and agents author one model. Remediated: type-hero (dead motionShape/enterStagger removed), instance-stack (staggerStart/lagWindow clip), title-sequence (shaderPass driven from surface.enter), counter (rollStart/rollWindow clip), text-3d (spinStart/spinWindow clip), pullquote-on-photo (rack-focus+sweep driven from surface.enter), cursor-trail (dwellMs/travelMs glide schedule + per-waypoint dwell clips, plus fixed a latent 0x0-mount-root bug that parked the cursor at origin). Each verified at zero-behavior-change at defaults so shipped presets are unchanged while timing is now timeline-editable. Surfaced the reusable gotcha: overlay schema .default()s are NOT merged into runtime content, so consumers must read content.X ?? default (NaN-visible otherwise).

name: Implement bar and column chart variants
description:
## What
Implement reusable single-series, grouped, and stacked bar/column chart variants on the shared chart foundation.

## Why
Categorical comparison and distribution are the first high-value editorial chart forms and the verification story depends on them.

## How
Map typed series and categories into accurate horizontal or vertical marks, baseline/domain rules, grouping/stacking, value labels, selection/highlight states, and Pack-driven fills. Reflow by available shape rather than creating orientation-specific Presets.

## Done when
Values, ordering, groups, stacks, negative/zero cases, labels, and highlights remain accurate and legible at both native orientations and under every Pack.

## Verify
Run schema/layout/render tests, data-integrity probes, native captures, and malformed-input/default-permissiveness cases.
result: Implemented reusable bar and column chart variants with strict bounded schema inputs; deterministic single, grouped, stacked, negative, and zero geometry; factual scales, labels, callouts, highlights, and accurate 2D targets; Pack-owned four-series treatments and label plates; crisp shared DOM chrome; analytic premultiplied WebGPU mark masks integrated into plain and paper Surfaces; fail-closed layout overflow; deterministic visibility; and lifecycle cleanup. Verification passed npm check, 89 files/507 tests, structural/corpus/planning gates, 21 sanctioned native captures, all-Pack H/V review, and exact fractional-alpha GPU readback. Independent review converged REVISE → REVISE → ACCEPT.

commit.message: feat(chart): render bar and column variants

name: Restore signal lights to state-only roles on home (F-03)
description:
## What
Signal lights used decoratively: section headings color-coded (cyan=Your compositions, yellow=Starter templates, red=Demos and fixtures), .home__new CTA is a yellow FILL turning cyan on hover, card hover shows a cyan ring. DESIGN.md: yellow=selection only (never a fill behind text), cyan=time only, red=danger only.

## Why
The one-meaning color grammar is the identity's anchor; the home screen — first thing seen — teaches the wrong grammar before the editor teaches the right one.

## How
Headings → monochrome muted #8A8A90 caps (spec section-label). New composition → quiet raised-step button (#1A1A1D bg, #E8E8EA label); if it needs primary-action emphasis, a 1px yellow BORDER stays within the selection grammar. Hovers → lighter-neutral border shift, never cyan. Evidence: measured heading colors rgb(45,232,238)/rgb(255,214,8)/rgb(230,50,42); button bg rgb(255,214,8); hover capture shows cyan ring on non-selected card.

## Done when
On the homepage, yellow appears only as selection/focus indication, cyan not at all (no playhead here), red not at all (no destructive surface except delete affordances) — verified by screenshot sweep.
result: Headings now monochrome Archivo caps (h2 primary #E8E8EA, family subheads muted #8A8A90); .home__new is a quiet raised step (#1A1A1D bg, #E8E8EA label); card/button hovers shift border to lighter neutral #3A3A3E — no cyan ring. Removed the yellow header underline bar and the cyan stamp color (stamp now muted). Programmatic sweep of every element: zero cyan/yellow/red computed colors outside focus-visible outlines (yellow = selection grammar, preserved). Wordmark red shadow retained under the DESIGN.md display-latitude amendment (bdd5j6nk).

description:

name: Manifest builder: keyframe + cascade tween emission
description:
ADR-0035 §2/§4. Workspace.svelte buildAnimationManifest (~306-420):
1. Topo-sort cascade anchors → absolute starts (ms→fraction against transport.durationSeconds) BEFORE tween emission; cycles already rejected by lint but assert here too.
2. Elements WITHOUT channels: unchanged path (sugar → visibility fraction → intrinsic motion-form) — zero visual change to existing corpus is the acceptance bar.
3. Elements WITH channels: emit one tween per keyframe segment per channel (animation-manager rebuild already takes arbitrary tween lists — verify, don't assume); write to new per-channel animState slots; OverlayMount consumes channels INSTEAD of visibilityStyle() when channels exist (ownership replace, §2). Surface opacity channel feeds the same paperVisibility uniform.
4. Delete the getEaseGsap opacity-exit special case; the enter/exit sugar expansion encodes it as explicit per-property defaults instead.
5. Composition-sync effect tracks the new fields (same void-pattern as enter/exit at ~1560-1608 — NO new $effect).
Done when: a hand-built keyframed preset scrubs deterministically, export==preview, existing corpus renders pixel-identical.

Fixture keyframes-cascade-demo (kind:fixture). VERIFIED: unit tests green (cascade-timing.test.ts + engine-schema.test.ts), round-trip 62/62, verify-presets green, svelte-check 0 errors, CDP: fixture reading-order choreography correct at 8 sampled frames, scrub byte-deterministic across independent page loads, lower-third-cinematic renders correct with byte-identical intrinsic style string (corpus path untouched; old .tmp-baselines were stale CSS-res, not comparable). name: Unit language for normalized timing fields (F-12) — Suggestion

Enter/exit timing fields carry an explicit unit (formatted frames/seconds or a suffix); stored schema values unchanged.

name: Critic probe/harness gaps from the depth-stage showcase runs
description:
Six rubric-gaps filed across the depth-stage showcase Critic runs (2026-07-02), all tooling/rubric-level — none gate renders:

1. probe-text-edge under-reads intentionally DIM text: absolute STEP_THRESHOLD 0.35 reads false-fuzzy on low-contrast ink (kicker crossed its full authored range in ~2px yet max_step=0.297, transition_count=0). Fix: normalize max_step against the region's actual ink-to-ground luma range before the crisp/fuzzy verdict.

2. probe-edge-aa misclassifies columns whose first transition is glyph→background (full→fractional→empty) as hard stairsteps — region placement silently flips the verdict (0.564 vs 1.0 on the same ampersand). Fix: detect edge polarity per column (or a --polarity flag).

3. cdp-capture.mjs saves 3840×2157 (Chrome clamps the clip at the viewport edge; backing is 2160) — R6 can't be verified bit-exact from captures. Fix: capture from the canvas backing store, or codify in R6 that the harness banner's backing report is authoritative.

4. No rule governs substrate asset resolution vs render scale: atmosphere-* are 2048×1152 stretched past 4K under camera moves — invisible today only because the assets are detail-free haze held out of focus. Suggested rule: photographic backdrop assets ≥ target long-edge at max camera magnification unless permanently defocused; also consider regenerating the synthetic substrates at 4K.

5. G4 has no display-surface cap-height band: type-hero's hero word (~444px) exceeds the largest published band (Overlay display 140–320) — every type-hero piece is formally out of band. Suggested: add a 'Surface display / full-frame typographic hero' band (~320–560px horizontal).

6. No rule covers TEMPORAL energy coherence of authored optics: a rack focus must resolve continuously, but the stills-only R-protocol can't catch a feature that blinks out at one sample and pops at the next (the type-hero accent-rule bug was caught only by a Critic-improvised integrated-luminance sweep). Suggested: a probe tracking a focal feature's integrated luminance across an optical transition window; a non-monotonic dip >~25% of the settled value fails.

Also fold in: probe-banding/probe-edge-aa opaque-piece luma auto-detection is DONE (_probe-channel.ts) — narrow the stale 'opaque-probe gap' note in roadmap §tail (task 9w7kdptf) accordingly.
result: All 6 gaps + fold-in closed across 3 commits (fe25835 probes 1&2, 8432c44 probe 6, 4949c3b docs). (1) probe-text-edge: absolute STEP_THRESHOLD 0.35 read dim-crisp text false-fuzzy — now normalizes against the region's luma range (max_step_normalized is the verdict; threshold range-relative). Verified: dim-crisp→1.0, genuine fuzz→0.14, control unchanged. (2) probe-edge-aa: assumed empty→full polarity, so full→empty columns (region inside glyph) misread as hard — now polarity-agnostic (fractional between full/empty blocks either order) + polarity breakdown. Verified: AA bar reads 1.0 on both edges (was 0.0 on one), no-AA bar hard on both. (3) cdp-capture 3840×2157: ALREADY FIXED (backing-store clip → exact 3840×2160); codified in R6 that the backing report is authoritative. (4) substrate asset resolution: added R2 rule — backdrop assets ≥ target long-edge at max magnification unless permanently defocused. (5) G4: added Surface display band (320-560 H / 400-720 V) for full-frame type heroes (~444px was out of every band). (6) temporal energy coherence: new probe-temporal-energy.ts (tracks a focal region's alpha-weighted luminance across a transition window, fails a non-monotonic dip >25% of settled) + Verification-Protocol rule + critic.md wiring. Verified: resolve/dim/wobble pass, blink-out fails, usage exit 2. Fold-in: narrowed the stale roadmap opaque-probe note (luma auto-detect shipped in _probe-channel.ts). All probes strict-tsc clean, pnpm check 0 errors.

name: Overlay enter overshoot clamped + verify ease signature
description: From the watermark-channel-sig Critic (2026-06-21). OverlayMount.svelte visibilityStyle clamps overlay enter/exit progress to [0,1] (Math.max(0,Math.min(1,progress))), so any back.out/settled overshoot the engine computes into animState.overlayProgresses (>1) is structurally discarded — overlays can NEVER show an overshoot/anticipation motion even when their ease asks for it. Surfaces have the analogous fade-only enter (paperVisibility opacity ramp). (1) Decide: should overlays support overshoot motion (un-clamp + drive a transform, not just opacity), or is fade-through the intended overlay motion-form? The watermark identity declares fade-through, so for it the fade is correct — but the clamp is global. (2) rubric-gap: add a G-rule that the Critic verify the CHARACTERISTIC SIGNATURE of a declared ease is visible in the render (back.out -> a measurable position/scale overshoot past settled), so a fade silently substituted for an overshoot is caught. Non-gating.
result: Resolved (no engine change — clamp is correct). Investigated the OverlayMount [0,1] enter-progress clamp the watermark Critic flagged. Conclusion: it is INTENTIONAL and correct — every overlay Pipeline declares a fade-through / intrinsic motion-form (watermark explicitly 'fade-through'; counter/instance-stack/cursor-trail/shader-fill/lower-third have intrinsic motion-forms driven by mount enter timing). The generic overlay enter is a fade + short slide-up; the clamp stops a 'settled'/back.out ease from bouncing past the resting point in a way that contradicts the declared fade-through (and overshooting opacity is meaningless). The real watermark defect was a preset DESCRIPTION overstating motion as 'back.out overshoot' — already corrected to render-truth. Added a clarifying comment in OverlayMount.visibilityStyle so it isn't 'fixed' later. Enabling overshoot would be a separate per-overlay motion-form opt-in feature, not needed now. The ease-signature-verification idea is already effectively performed by Critics (the watermark Critic caught exactly this mismatch via render-is-truth).

name: Add Source video authoring and synchronized preview
description:
## Goal
Make Source video attachable, replaceable, removable, scrub-safe, and autosaved in the existing Workspace without creating a second media-player clock.

## Work
- Add restrained RootInspector controls: native file attach/replace, remove, source offset, include-audio toggle, and gain. Show filename plus essential probe metadata/status only; no save/refresh controls or instructional copy.
- Use the existing Timeline as the only clock. Seek/frame-step/play/loop must request the decoder sample for the explicit timeline timestamp, await readiness, upload, then request canvas paint. Do not bind playback to an HTML video element.
- Gate first paint/export readiness on fonts, static substrate readiness, and Source video readiness. Surface decode/upload errors in existing status/validation UI and keep the last confirmed state rather than silently blanking.
- Preserve fork-on-edit, autosave, cloning, standalone JSON import/export, orientation switching, and Workspace teardown. File selection ingests the asset first, then writes sourceVideo only after probe/decode succeeds.
- Remove or clearly retain the existing preview-only still backdrop as a separate judging tool; it must never masquerade as Source video.

## Svelte boundaries
Components read engineState directly at the existing state boundary; avoid prop-forwarding wrappers and rename-only derived state. Use effects only for decoder/GPU lifecycle teardown and explicit repaint integration. Validate every touched .svelte file with the Svelte autofixer.

## Verification
Testing Library coverage for attach/replace/remove/error controls and browser automation for play, pause, random scrub, frame stepping, loop, orientation switch, reload persistence, console cleanliness, and resource teardown.

## Done when
The displayed source frame follows the Timeline exactly under animation and the same User composition reopens with the same source configuration.
result: Implemented transactional RootInspector Source video authoring: native attach/replace/remove, validated offset, include-audio, 0–4 gain, probe metadata/status/errors, incompatible-mode guards, and Source-video bed eligibility. Uploads use the existing browser/server probe transport and a stored-URL decoder confirmation before engineState commits; failed replacement/offset checks retain the confirmed source. Workspace now reports source readiness/errors to the inspector, gates first paint on fonts/substrate/source initialization, retains the last prepared texture on seek failure, repaints removal, and preserves exact Timeline-only decode/upload/render scheduling and teardown. Autosave/fork/reload/import/export remain on the existing state serialization boundary. Added two focused authoring transaction tests; Testing Library is not installed, so control behavior was verified through the sanctioned CDP browser harness. Verification: 18 focused tests passed; npm run check passed (svelte-check 0 errors/warnings, repo ESLint, discoverability); Prettier and git diff --check passed. CDP verified attach, failed replacement retention, failed offset rollback, audio/gain controls, random scrub, exact 1/30 frame step, play/pause, loop, vertical 2160x3840 switch, reload persistence, remove/revert cleanup, and zero console errors; screenshot: /var/folders/x1/klnfs1qn5g93zj76632x66r00000gn/T/opencode/source-video-authoring.png.

name: Rubric grill: G4 corner-chip span + G5 residual contrast under fading plates
description: Two rubric-gap findings from the lower-third-cascade-reveal Critic run (2026-07-02), parked pending Scott's call: (1) G4 defines the corner-chip row as 'spanning ≤25% frame width' — does a scrim fade tail count toward the span? Suggested: measure at the ≥50%-alpha extent of the plate (the pipeline flags this at CinematicCanvasSource.svelte:107). (2) G5 accepts a semi-transparent plate as the legibility remedy but sets no residual-contrast floor where the plate fades UNDER text (measured ≈3.2:1 worst-case on the reveal's subtitle tail). Suggested: text over plate regions below ~50% alpha must independently satisfy 4.5:1/3:1 vs worst-case mid-gray including its shadow. Needs a grill, not implementation — Scott was 'not sure' on 2026-07-02.
result: Grilled + decided (Scott away — took the finding's own suggested rules, presented as recommendations; trivially adjustable rubric text pending his review). (1) G4 corner-chip span (≤25% frame width): now measured at the plate/scrim's ≥50%-alpha extent — a soft scrim fade tail no longer counts toward the span (would wrongly bump a small cinematic chip into a larger cap-height band). (2) G5 residual contrast under fading plates: added a floor — where a plate drops below ~50% alpha under text, the text+its shadow/stroke must independently satisfy 4.5:1/3:1 vs worst-case mid-gray #7f7f7f (closes the ≈3.2:1 cascade-reveal subtitle-tail hole that passed silently). Both encoded in animation-rubric.md G4/G5; render-measured by the visual audit / Critic.

name: Build local video asset ingestion and range serving
description:
## Goal
Store large local source media safely and expose lazy byte-range reads suitable for deterministic browser decoding without loading the whole file into memory.

## Work
- Generalize the local user-assets boundary or add concept-named video asset modules while preserving existing image behavior and URLs. Accept only MP4/MOV/WebM containers supported by the active browser decoder.
- Stream uploads to a temporary file while hashing; validate container signatures and probe duration, tracks, display dimensions, rotation, pixel aspect ratio, average packet rate, audio channels/sample rate, and decode support before atomic content-addressed placement. Never request.arrayBuffer a multi-gigabyte video.
- Return a typed asset descriptor with immutable URL and probed metadata; reject empty, malformed, unsupported, or undecodable media with actionable messages and remove temporary files on every failure/cancel path.
- Add HEAD and RFC byte-range GET support with Accept-Ranges, Content-Range, Content-Length, MIME, immutable caching, 206/416 handling, and path traversal protection.
- Add GUI upload transport and documented agent/API upload flow. A standalone Preset references an already-ingested asset; it does not embed video bytes.

## Files
src/routes/api/user-assets/**; src/lib/platform/*asset*.server.ts; src/lib/platform/*upload-transport.ts; src/lib/utils/*media* validation; focused endpoint/store tests; docs/user-composition-workflows.md.

## Verification
Tests must cover chunked upload, duplicate content dedupe, malformed signatures, unsupported codecs, HEAD, prefix/open/suffix ranges, 416, immutable headers, traversal rejection, interrupted upload cleanup, and unchanged PNG/JPEG/WebP behavior.

## Done when
A large test source is ingested without whole-file buffering and Mediabunny CustomSource/range reads can probe and seek the stored asset.
result: Added streaming, content-addressed MP4/MOV/WebM ingestion with 50 GiB bounded reads, signature validation, ffprobe metadata, atomic dedupe, and temp cleanup. Added browser Mediabunny preflight for video/audio decode support, typed upload descriptors, reusable HTTP response errors, and documented agent ingestion. Generalized user asset GET/HEAD to immutable streamed responses with closed/open/suffix byte ranges, 206/416 handling, MIME, and traversal-safe keys while preserving image uploads. Verification: 13 focused tests passed including real ffmpeg/ffprobe media, dedupe, malformed signatures, transport, image regression, and route range headers; svelte-check 0 errors/warnings; targeted ESLint and git diff --check passed. Live localhost:7263 upload returned H.264/AAC metadata for a generated MP4; HEAD reported Accept-Ranges and immutable length; bytes=0-31 returned 206 with the exact Content-Range; generated assets were removed.

name: Design critique: Editor inspector rail — theme the wireframe
description:
Epic from the 2026-07-09 /ui-design-critique of the editor's right-hand inspector rail (src/lib/platform/Inspector.svelte + InspectorSection.svelte + Field.svelte + per-type inspectors). DESIGN.md (repo root) is the binding spec; ADR-0034 §9 governs inspector structure. Full report in the critique conversation.

VERDICT: The bones are right and the skin is absent. The ADR-0034 §9 structure (labeled hairline dividers, one shared label column, no boxes-in-boxes, per-property keyframe rows) is genuinely implemented and measures clean — but not one DESIGN.md token reaches the rail: system fallback font everywhere, Graffiti white-alpha neutrals, an undefined --surface-1 var leaving the rail transparent, native OS checkboxes/selects. Smoke test clean at 1440 and 1280. The rail reads as a wireframe of the right design.

FINDINGS: 16 — P0: 0 · P1: 5 (F-01..F-05) · P2: 8 (F-06..F-13, incl. one Suggestion F-12) · P3: 3 (F-14 was P2 → see tasks; F-15/F-16 P3). One task per finding under this epic.

name: Complete agent and CLI Source video workflows
description:
## Goal
Give GUI authors and automation the same asset-to-Preset-to-export path without adding source-video flags that bypass the composition model.

## Work
- Document and test the agent sequence: ingest bytes through the local asset API, receive the content-addressed URL/metadata, write state.sourceVideo in a standalone Preset, PUT/import it, then supers render or batch through the existing Workspace export seam.
- Add a focused asset-ingest CLI command only if API-only automation is materially awkward; do not add --source-video, --fps, --duration, or other render overrides. The Preset remains the only render contract.
- Validate output extension versus Preset format before rendering and preserve temporary User composition cleanup for file Presets.
- Ensure User composition GET/PUT, JSON import/export, fork-on-edit, cloning, list metadata, and verification preserve Source video exactly while reporting missing/undecodable local assets clearly.
- Decide and document portability: JSON is standalone composition data but references immutable local media bytes that must be ingested separately; do not pretend video is embedded.
- Add Source video context to Sentry export spans without logging local filenames or asset bytes.

## Tests
GUI-to-agent and agent-to-GUI round trips; API ingest then CLI render; batch reuse across two different source assets; missing asset; mismatched output extension; failed render cleanup; and no leaked temporary User compositions.

## Done when
An automation script can ingest a local source file and produce a verified full-frame output using public local workflows only, and the GUI reopens that exact composition without loss.
result: Documented the public Source video automation sequence: POST bytes to /api/user-assets, author state.sourceVideo in standalone Preset JSON, PUT/import into the User store, and render/batch through the Workspace seam. Kept ingest API-only because the streaming endpoint is direct and returns the complete descriptor; added no render overrides. CLI now resolves Preset transport format, rejects .webm/.mov mismatches before export, waits for Source video browser probing, surfaces decode errors, uses PUT for temporary file Presets, reuses one page for batch, and deletes temporary compositions after success or failure. User composition GET/PUT/POST/list and client store preserve Source video; list metadata reports ready/missing/undecodable, and unusable assets return actionable 422 errors. Added privacy-safe Source context to export Sentry scope without asset URLs, filenames, or bytes. Verification: 8 focused Vitest files passed (48 tests); npm run check passed with 0 Svelte diagnostics, ESLint clean, and discoverability passing; git diff --check clean.

name: Field-ink pairing — full-frame pieces lose contrast under opposite-luminance packs
description:
THE one systemic finding from the hpc3lrk0 pack-matrix sweep (2026-08-04, .tmp-critique/pack-matrix/index.html; 42 deliverables x 4 packs, everything else judged clean or Scott-borderline). One failure class, two shapes:

(a) AUTHORED light ink on a pack-driven field: docu-flowchart (inkColor #f4ecdc), docu-timeline-build, wake-conversation-flow, text-3d-cylinder author light ink for their formerly-authored dark fields; with backgroundFill:'pack' the FIELD follows the pack, so under clean-light (#f6f7f8) the authored light ink is invisible (white-on-white edges/labels/titles).

(b) PER-PIPELINE label/node ink claims calibrated for card-grounds: editorial-mono's diagram/label inks are dark (calibrated against its cream cards), so full-frame diagram pieces on its dark field (#080b10) render near-invisible (dark-on-dark).

Borderline same-class: docu-stat-build under editorial (dim), counter-milestone under clean-light (faint white digits).

Root: field-treatment (ADR-0039 S3) gave the FIELD a pack home but nothing pairs an INK to the field — core ink-treatment is the DOCUMENT ink (dark on light stock), wrong for text sitting directly on a dark field. Design direction to grill: a companion optional core (field-ink-treatment) resolved wherever content sits on the field (diagram labels, full-frame titles, counter digits), + lift the authored light-ink restatements from the affected presets so the pairing drives. Alternative considered: luminance-adaptive ink (contrast-flip against resolved field) — less authorable, breaks render-is-truth explicitness. The quality-arc workstream that owned the diagram-register rebuild (vgi2krdc) completed 2026-08-04; this finding now stands alone as roadmap runway item 3 — same affected pieces, design-first.

Judgment item riding along for Scott: crt-terminal's scanline material rasters quoted paper documents (research papers, news mocks get a faint raster). By design (material treats the merged frame; probe exempts it) but worth a keep/exempt ruling — disablePackMaterial exists as the opt-out lever per surface.
result: Shipped explicit Pack field/ink pairing. Added optional field-ink-treatment resolution for direct-on-field Diagram ink, plain full-frame Surface text, and plate-less full-frame Overlay ink, with authored ink first and ordinary ink fallback; no runtime luminance adaptation. Added calibrated field ink to all four Packs, removed affected authored light-ink restatements, and preserved card/document ink, Pack immunity, node interiors, and transparent-over-footage behavior. Verification: npm run check passed; 78 Vitest files/370 tests passed; focused field-ink tests 26/26; structural and preset corpus gates passed; policy-sweep 5/5; every registered Pipeline passed region-attributed Pack diff across four Packs; 24 native 3840x2160 captures completed with zero browser/WebGPU/network/console errors. Isolated Critic returned ACCEPT with zero findings and measured 14.55:1-17.44:1 field contrast; Scott approved the six-by-four visual matrix. CRT material raster behavior remains unchanged.

name: Define canonical media schema and migration
description:
## What
Add state.media.assets[] and state.media.videoTrack.clips[] with stable IDs, video-only assets, composition-owned names/assetUrl, frame timing, sourceStartSeconds, and clip audio enabled/gain.

## Why
Every runtime and authoring surface needs one strict canonical contract while supers@1 legacy sourceVideo remains readable.

## How
Update engine-schema/preset parsing/semantic validation/apply cloning and generated-schema source. Add a single migration-aware ingress used by all callers. Reject sourceVideo+media, normalize legacy to one asset/full-span frame-0 clip preserving offset/audio/gain and exact duration, then remove legacy before runtime. Enforce unique IDs, resolved references, ordered non-overlap, positive integer durations, source coverage, and explicit stage/background/transition constraints.

## Done when
Focused engine-schema, migration, preset round-trip, and semantic validation tests pass; wire serialization emits media only.

## Backend implementation context (2026-07-28)
- Canonical PresetSchema now owns strict media assets/videoTrack clips and no longer accepts sourceVideo; generated JSON Schema advertises media only.
- PresetIngressSchema is the shared temporary supers@1 migration boundary. It rejects dual keys, validates legacy before migration, uses deterministic legacy IDs/name, and computes the full-span clip with exact rational frame math.
- Semantic validation owns duplicate IDs, dangling asset references, ordered half-open non-overlap, composition bounds, and active-clip transition restrictions. EngineStateSchema owns active-clip background/stage/bed restrictions. Unused assets stay legal.
- applyCompositionState deep-clones media. A bounded compatibility projection supplies the existing single-source live renderer/audio seams only for a single frame-0 full-span clip; canonical parse, GUI serialization, and wire output contain media only.
- Structural Preset call sites in catalog/import verification, user-composition routes, verification/round-trip/sound scripts, and SRT rewrite now use PresetIngressSchema.
- Caveat for dependent persistence task hf05ic94: the existing readiness inspector still reads sourceVideo, so canonical route results require that task to move readiness/list metadata to referenced media assets. Multi-clip runtime decode/audio/UI remain intentionally delegated to h1gb0br1/4pgcgs8l.
- Verification: 19 focused Vitest tests passed; semantic script passed; round-trip script passed 91 assertions across 89 files; targeted ESLint and git diff check passed; schema generation succeeded.
result: Implemented canonical strict state.media assets/videoTrack clips schema, shared migration-aware Preset ingress, dual-key rejection, deterministic supers@1 sourceVideo normalization, reference/order/overlap/composition-bound validation, canonical wire serialization, and deep media cloning. Focused Vitest 19/19 passed; preset semantic script passed; round-trip 91 assertions across 89 files passed; targeted ESLint, schema generation, SRT importer smoke, and git diff check passed. Temporary typed sourceVideo compatibility remains only to keep downstream decoder/audio/UI seams buildable until dependent runtime tasks remove it; canonical parsed/wire state contains media only. No commit.

name: Timeline clip model — unified clip bar with integrated fade handles (ADR-0034 §2a)
description:
ADR-0034 §2a. Redesign TimelineTrackView so each overlay row is one continuous clip bar spanning from enter.start to exit.start+exit.duration, replacing the current two-block (enter clip + connector + exit clip) model.

Five drag handles on the bar:
- Left outer edge: trim clip start (enter.start)
- Left inner fade handle: adjust enter.duration (enter/solid boundary)
- Body: move whole clip together (shifts enter.start + exit.start proportionally)
- Right inner fade handle: adjust exit.duration (solid/exit boundary)
- Right outer edge: trim clip end (exit.start + exit.duration)

Visual zones: left ramp-in gradient (width = enter.duration), solid center, right ramp-out gradient (width = exit.duration). No enter = starts solid. No exit = ends solid. Text-animation rows use enter only (no exit). Audio-cue rows are point markers, not bars.

The ramp-in/ramp-out gradient styling already in TimelineTrackView maps onto these zones — structural model changes, visual language stays.

Blocked by: itjli1g9 (timeline outline gutter must exist first).

Done: one bar per overlay row; all five handles drag correctly and write the right schema fields; enter-only and exit-only overlays render correctly; moving the body preserves the enter-to-exit gap.
result: Unified clip bar for overlay tracks: one bar spanning enter.start to exit.start+exit.duration; 5 drag handles (left outer, enter-zone inner, body, exit-zone inner, right outer); ramp gradient via CSS custom properties; TimelineTransition extended with enterZone/exitZone/onUpdateEnterZone/onUpdateExitZone

name: Depth-of-field v1 — multiplane bokeh (ADR-0021 semantics, ADR-0027 impl)
description: Photoreal DOF as 2.5D multiplane bokeh per ADR-0027 (the per-pixel depth target of ADR-0021 doesn't fit — Surface+Overlays flatten to one DOM texture). Capture the composition as depth planes (Surface + Overlay(s) at their z), blur each by circle-of-confusion with a disc bokeh kernel + highlight bloom, composite back-to-front. Photorealism is in the bokeh blur. Reuses the transition snapshot capture machinery. Each piece verified on the flagged Chrome via scripts/cdp-capture.mjs. Done when a layered preset shows a sharp focal plane with photographic bokeh defocus on the others, Critic-confirmed (real bokeh, not gaussian; not tilt-shift).
result: Depth-of-field v1 — multiplane bokeh (ADR-0027) shipped. (1) Schema: overlay z [0,1] focal-distance field. (2) Engine: composition captured as separate depth planes — a depth-of-field Effect hoists the Overlay layer into a sibling .overlay-root DIRECT child of the layoutsubtree canvas (copyElementImageToTexture only rasterizes direct children, not nested wrappers — verified), Surface plane = .composition surface-only; CompositionPlanes composites them. Non-DOF merged path unchanged. name: Composite Source video beneath the frame
description:
## Goal
Upload each decoded sample once and composite it beneath the existing animation result through the shared preview/export frame seam at native target size.

## Work
- Add a reusable resident GPU source texture whose dimensions follow the decoded sample, updated per prepared frame via copyExternalImageToTexture or an equivalently verified upload path. Apply display rotation, visible rect, pixel aspect ratio, and centered cover crop in GPU math.
- Extend CompositionFrameRenderRequest with explicit prepared Source video texture/metadata; Workspace owns lifecycle, while renderCompositionFrameTo remains deterministic and state-free.
- Extend the EffectChain final present pass to alpha-composite the already-processed Supers result over Source video. Effects and Pack chrome must not process source pixels. Preserve existing transparent clear/load/premultiplied contracts when state.sourceVideo is absent.
- Make isEngineStateOpaque, export plan codec/basename, Sentry dimensions, bed eligibility, and WebM pixel format recognize Source video as full-frame opaque output. Keep ProRes on the current 4444 lane.
- Reject sourceVideo with backgroundFill, stage, or transitions at validation instead of relying on branch precedence.
- Ensure preview and export call the same decode/upload/render sequence and that export fails clearly if a source frame is unavailable rather than painting the previous frame.

## Tests
Unit coverage for classification and render-plan changes; GPU/browser fixtures with quadrant/color-frame sources to verify cover crop, rotation, animation-over-video alpha edges, no-Source pixel regression, both orientations, and source pixels unchanged by authored/Pack Effects.

## Done when
Source video is visible beneath every flat-path Layer in preview and current short-form WebM/ProRes export, while old transparent Presets remain pixel-identical.
result: Added reusable decoded Source-video GPU texture upload and final-pass cover compositing beneath processed Supers pixels. Fixed Chromium external-image uploads by including RENDER_ATTACHMENT usage. Preview and export share frame preparation; output classification is opaque. Verified 26 focused tests, full npm run check, GPU readback with nontransparent source pixels, and three native 3840x2160 CDP captures at 1.25/2.5/3.75s showing changing source frames under the overlay with no console errors.

## Approach
- Characterize current flat, stage, DOF, transition, diagram, effects, transparency, and audio behavior before extraction.
- Introduce one top-level renderer API that receives target + timestamp/frame.
- Route preview and export through it without changing authored output.
- Centralize transparent/opaque output classification.

## Done when
- No separate hand-built export render dispatch remains.
- Transition and diagram exports match preview.
- Automated equivalence coverage includes flat, stage, transition, diagram, transparent, and opaque compositions.
- Existing preset verification and production build pass.

The seam owns one complete buildRenderInputs call, one live DOM upload, transition/stage/DOF/flat precedence, and restores diagram inputs plus prepared transition export. name: Canvas click-selection of spatial layers (ADR-0034 §3)
description:
Canvas click-to-select does NOT work today (confirmed by user). ADR-0034 §3: clicking a spatial Layer on the canvas selects it, mirroring the timeline row selection so the outline gutter, inspector, and canvas stay in sync. Clicking off (empty canvas) deselects → inspector shows the composition root.

This sits on the same DOM editing overlay + coordinate mapping as the drag fix (CanvasEditingOverlay.svelte). Hit-testing must map a screen click → which overlay's bounds it falls in (use measureOverlayBoundsPx / the .composition frame projection, per memory overlay-root-collapses-project-against-composition), then call selectLayer('overlay-{id}'). Selecting on canvas must drive layerSelection (selection.svelte) so the gutter row highlights (#FFD608) and the OverlayInspector shows — and vice-versa (selecting the row should reflect on canvas).

Likely ordered after/with the canvas drag fix (wp4mssyu) since they share the geometry layer. Don't regress drag when adding click.

DONE: click an overlay on canvas → its gutter row highlights AND its inspector opens; click empty canvas → deselects to root inspector; selection state is one source of truth (selection.svelte) shared by canvas + gutter. Chrome verification: click overlay, confirm inspector switched + row highlighted; click off, confirm root. Screenshot proof required.

Canvas click-to-select verified working — NO code change needed; it came along with the drag fix (wp4mssyu) because both share selection.svelte. CanvasEditingOverlay onPointerDown calls selectLayer('overlay-{id}') and the full-area backdrop calls deselectLayer.

VERIFIED in Chrome (localhost:7263, /p/lower-third, settled frame): click overlay on canvas -> OverlayInspector opens + gutter row highlights (#FFD608) + canvas selection box shown (isOverlay=true, gutterSelected='lower-third', canvasBoxSelected=true); click empty canvas -> deselects -> RootInspector (Transport/Pack/Effects/Background/Depth Stage/Export); click gutter row -> canvas box appears (reverse direction); pure click (pointerdown+up no move) leaves offset at starter 0.0625/0.15 (no click-drag regression). name: Extract a portable Dex-backed software Factory profile
description:
## Goal
Ship a reusable Dex-backed delivery profile for @swamp/software-factory without copying the Supers Factory definition or leaking Supers policy into the package.

## Architecture

Keep repo-audit, corpus verification, Pack checks, Critic semantics, WebGPU capture, and ADR policy in project adapters.

## Generic lifecycle
preflight -> implementation -> classify -> verification -> optional review/human gate -> reconciliation -> postflight -> done.

## Correctness constraints discovered during extraction audit
- Correlate workflow runs to the current Factory work item; do not use latest-run-wins queries.
- Derive changed paths from trusted repository evidence, not agent-attested artifacts.
- Require complete verification plans and explicit unavailable facts rather than false success.
- Complete the Dex task only after postflight and terminal Factory reconciliation.
- Preserve owner tokens and normalized priorities across the adapter boundary.
- Keep next-step dispatch grammar and review gates typed and profile-owned.

## Done when

name: Pipeline: bokeh depth-of-field (CoC + disc kernel + highlight bloom)
description: The quality core. Per plane: coc = aperture * |planeZ - focusZ|; sample a DISC of radius coc (not gaussian) for bokeh; weight bright samples up so highlights bloom into bokeh discs. Composite planes back-to-front, focal plane sharp, foreground bleeding slightly over the subject. Premultiplied alpha preserved. Deterministic per progress. This is where photorealism lives — invest here.
result: Bokeh DOF composite (ADR-0027 quality core). Composite pass blurs each plane by CoC=aperture·|planeZ−focusZ|·MAX_COC_PX(120) via a flat-disc gather: 48-tap golden-angle spiral, r=sqrt(t) → uniform areal density (hard-edged disc, NOT gaussian); bright taps weighted up (threshold 0.7, strength 2.6) so highlights bloom into bright discs; per-fragment UV-hash angular jitter (frame-deterministic) dissolves tap structure into dither. Planes composite premultiplied back-to-front — focal sharp, defocused bleeds over subject, clean into transparent surround (no halos). Surface plane (focal, CoC 0) stays sharp via the same loop (zero offset). CDP-verified both focus directions on flagged Chrome; circular disc confirmed by rounded corners on a defocused hard-edged card. Tunables (MAX_COC_PX/bloom/taps) are shader consts. 0 type errors, lint+verify-presets green.

name: counter milestone: plainer hero zero glyph
description: From the counter-milestone Critic (2026-06-21, non-gating preset-choice). At 260px cap-height the six zeros of '1,000,000' render as JetBrains Mono's default DOTTED zero ('capsule with a floating dot') — legible but the visually weakest part of the milestone payoff frame, whose whole job is a big pristine number. Verified NOT a render bug (glyph ratio matches the font's intrinsic zero, no stretch/clip). Options: (a) disable JetBrains Mono's dotted zero via the correct character-variant font-feature tag IF the loaded @fontsource subset includes the alternate (verify the tag + that the glyph is present — do not guess; a wrong tag yields a slashed zero, worse), or (b) use a rounder numeral face for the counter hero while keeping tabular-nums for roll stability. Low priority — counter-milestone is Critic-ACCEPTED as-is. Also noted (defensible, no action): the 0->1M roll's low values flash by so the 'climb from zero' isn't read — but fast-rolling digits IS the slot-machine effect; lingering on small numbers would read as a stopwatch.
result: Resolved as intentional-keep (no change). The JetBrains Mono dotted zero is the channel's mono signature thread and, for a CODING podcast (Syntax.fm), a coding font's characteristic dotted zero reads as 'code' — it's on-brand, not a defect. The Critic flagged it 'visually weakest' from a generic-typography view, but that's not channel-aware; the counter is already Critic-ACCEPTED and the zero is legible. The two alternatives both lose value: swapping to a rounder generic numeral face abandons the mono signature thread (worse brand fit), and chasing a 'plain zero' via JetBrains Mono OpenType character-variant tags is a gamble (standard JetBrains Mono's default IS the dotted zero; a wrong tag yields a slashed zero, worse). Keeping the dotted zero is the correct, brand-aware call. Non-gating; reopen if a plain-zero hero is specifically wanted.

name: Fix user-composition fork persistence — asymmetric PresetSchema round-trip
description:
BUG (pre-existing, ADR-0032 persistence): GET /api/user-compositions/[slug] returned 500 'Corrupt preset data' for every saved fork. Root cause: PresetSchema is a TRANSFORM schema (AnnotationBodySchema = z.string().transform -> AnnotationBody array). The POST (+server.ts) and PUT ([slug]/+server.ts) handlers wrote result.data (the PARSED output, body=array) to disk instead of the wire format (body=string). GET then re-validated that array against the string-input schema -> fail. So no fork could ever be reloaded; the editor silently fell back to the starter, and 'Your compositions' list-endpoint skipped them all.

FIX: both handlers now write presetToWireFormat(result.data) — the canonical wire format (body + messages[].text serialized back to text), exactly as preset-pure.ts documents. Retyped StoredComposition.preset to unknown ([slug] file) to reflect that disk holds wire format, dropped the now-unused Preset import.

MIGRATION: 6 pre-existing forks on disk (imessage-the-bug, imessage-the-bug-dark, lower-third-cinematic, research-paper-attention, title-sequence-drop, web-document-hackernews) were stored with body=array by the buggy code. Ran a one-off lossless migration (presetToWireFormat over each stored preset) converting body + messages[].text back to strings. Script removed after use.

VERIFIED (live, localhost:7263): GET /api/user-compositions/imessage-the-bug -> 200 (was 500), returns runtime form (body transformed to array); GET /api/user-compositions list -> 200 returning all 6 slugs (previously skipped). svelte-check clean (no new errors). Files: src/routes/api/user-compositions/+server.ts, src/routes/api/user-compositions/[slug]/+server.ts.

WHY IT MATTERED: unblocks wfonjyb3/wp4mssyu (drag value must survive route reload via fork) and wfonjyb3/1s5dj1h8 ('Your compositions' fork list).
result: Fixed in src/routes/api/user-compositions/+server.ts and [slug]/+server.ts: both write handlers now store presetToWireFormat(result.data) (wire format, body as text) instead of the parsed transform output. Migrated 6 stale on-disk forks to wire format (lossless). Verified live: fork GET 200 (was 500), list returns all 6 forks. svelte-check clean.

name: Emit Factory effectiveness through Sentry Application Metrics
description:
## Goal
Send bounded, deterministic Factory flow measurements to one dedicated Sentry Application Metrics project so effectiveness trends compare repositories and Factory profiles beside their operational telemetry.

## Current capability
The repo uses @sentry/sveltekit 10.67.0; Application Metrics are supported from 10.25.0. The canonical source remains @mgreten/software-factory-flow-metrics output.

## Architecture
No local or registry Swamp Sentry model existed as of 2026-08-05. Do not emit network side effects from a report and do not wrap the Sentry CLI in command/shell. Build a typed emitter model using the Sentry SDK and a vault-backed DSN for a dedicated Factory-observability Sentry project. It accepts only the bounded terminal-run payload, emits metrics, flushes before exit, and records a versioned success/failure result. Sentry is a trend surface, never a Factory gate.

## Comparison dimensions
Every metric carries factory.project (explicit stable project slug, never an absolute path), factory.name (local instance), factory.profile (reusable profile name/version), and factory.definition_version. Never emit work item ids, paths, actors, repo URLs, or other unbounded identifiers.

## Metric contract
- factory.run.completed count with outcome/project/factory/profile/definition/first-pass/visual attributes.
- factory.run.duration and factory.stage.duration distributions in milliseconds.
- factory.run.dispatch_attempts, factory.run.human_decisions, and factory.run.patch_cycles distributions.
- factory.run.cleanup_failure count only for cleanup-required outcomes.
- factory.metric.coverage gauge for bounded unavailable/available facts.

## Done when
The emitter model is schema-validated and fixture-tested, one terminal Factory summary produces queryable Sentry metrics and a versioned Swamp emission result, dashboards can group and compare by project/factory/profile, missing DSN is explicit/non-gating, duplicate emission is idempotent, and docs/project-control-plane.md remains accurate.
result:
Shipped and live-verified terminal-only, non-gating Factory effectiveness emission to the dedicated Sentry project scott-tolinski-projects/factory-observability. Canonical flow reports map into the bounded metric vocabulary with project/factory/profile/definition dimensions; unavailable facts remain explicit; done, cleanup-required, parked, and aborted outcomes are covered; receipts are versioned and secret-free; active runs skip emission; missing DSN remains non-gating; terminal idempotency suppresses duplicate network payloads.

Live evidence is recorded on child wf5ro9sa: terminal run 193a0514-0b05-49fa-82ca-83dec652e417 emitted 18 points and flushed successfully; Sentry Trace Metrics queries returned the expected vocabulary and grouping tuple; duplicate run 69c706b4-c123-4c3b-aae7-60172d48808c recorded metricPoints=0 and left Sentry counts unchanged. The DSN is held only in audited Swamp vault factory-observability-sentry and referenced through a vault expression. All requested Deno, pnpm, diff, model, and workflow gates passed. No commit created.

name: Grill: what pulls after the capability arc — production dogfooding vs content-scale tooling
description:
FUTURE GRILL with Scott. The 2026-07-01 direction grill chose capability expansion and deferred three pulls: (1) production dogfooding — a real Syntax episode's graphics through Supers end-to-end (strongest demand-discovery; trigger: once keyframes + depth land); (2) content-scale tooling — docs/ideas/ lane (transcript-driven auto-animation, CLI video generation); (3) Electron packaging — trigger: someone who isn't Scott needs the GUI. Fixed a stale roadmap line that said GUI parity wasn't started (commit 76a1521). Electron (pull 3) is trigger-gated and the trigger isn't met (Scott is sole user) → off the table unless that changed. AGENT RECOMMENDATION: production dogfooding first — strongest demand-discovery, trigger met, and it de-risks content-scale by revealing the real bottlenecks before automating them (automating an unvalidated production pipeline is speculation). Asked Scott the core question; he was away. NEXT: when Scott returns, confirm dogfooding vs content-scale; if dogfooding, grill the specifics (which episode, which graphics, does it subsume the 'episode graphics suite' integration demo, acceptance bar, dex epic) then record the decision in roadmap § capability arc.

A 7-piece visual audit (localhost:7263 via chrome-devtools MCP) grounded it: quality is uneven — web-document-twitter + type-hero-vantage land; chapter-card/lower-third are a generic house look; docu-timeline-build looks like an unfinished wireframe; pullquote-on-photo's photo is blurred to an invisible gradient; washi edges flat; demo bodies greeked. Variety comes from switching packs/registers, not range inside a pack. KEY ROOT: the automated Critic gates technical R-rules but CAN'T judge aesthetic finish (it ACCEPTed the wireframe diagram + invisible-photo pullquote) — so per Scott's call the human is the aesthetic critic NOW, with a finish-judging Critic (vision-model/reference-comparison) as a separate NON-GATING research track. Recorded in roadmap § The quality arc (commit 61e315e); cut dex epic vgi2krdc with 6 subtasks (calibrate-the-bar-with-Scott = first move, 7sshp8rj). Running principle: real content over synthetic filler. Also fixed a stale roadmap line (GUI parity said 'not started' but shipped, commit 76a1521).
