name: Newspaper halftone chews mid-luma chip ink (verified NOT fixed by immunity)
description: 6ltfmkwx's task text hypothesized partial immunity would fix the clean-light chip-label pixelation (2026-07-13) as a side effect. VERIFIED FALSE at native 4K (commit b550e9e): the chip PLATE renders clean, but the label ink lands in the halftone dot screen's mid-tone band — newspaper-physics fires smoothstep(0.05,0.30)x(1-smoothstep(0.70,0.92)) on luminance, and clean-light's newspaper.kicker-ink #5b6472 (mid-luma slate) gets fully dot-screened inside every glyph. Syntax never showed it because its chip ink #1a1612 sits below the 0.05 dark cutoff. The chip is claimable channel chrome ON the document — it should not receive the document's print physics. Fix direction: exclude chrome pixels from the halftone screen (the pass's saturation mask already skips saturated overlay pixels, but chip GLYPHS are desaturated slate on a saturated plate — needs a neighborhood-saturation or region-aware gate; weigh against body-text-over-highlight which SHOULD stay halftoned). Repro: CDP_PACK=clean-light node scripts/cdp-capture.mjs server-renders-again, zoom the ENGINEERING chip. Interim authoring dodge: packs can keep chip ink outside 0.30-0.70 luma.
result: Fixed in newspaper-physics: 8-tap 12px chrome-neighborhood saturation veto on the halftone screen — desaturated label ink inside saturated chrome (chip glyphs) no longer dot-screens; per-pixel gate still catches saturated inks. Verified at native 4K under clean-light (glyphs fully solid; 4-tap version left junction specks, axis ring closed them) and counter-checked under syntax (title solid, body halftone/bleed intact). Identity halftone dimension updated with the chrome exclusion + chip probe expectation. Cost documented: body ink within ~12px of a saturated mark boundary skips the screen (hairline halo).

name: Marker grammar v2: color-agnostic + explicit start/end markers
description: Real-editor feedback (2026-07-15, ReachyMini session): setting marker colors in Resolve is a huge pain and the purple family (Fuchsia/Purple/Lavender/Rose/Pink) is indistinguishable — color must be OUTPUT-only (Mint = synced, written by the sync), never required input. Editors also reach for an explicit START + END marker pair instead of dragging the head marker's duration. Fold into src/lib/utils/marker-sync.ts (+tests): (1) accept groups in any input color, identified by head note or conversational selection; (2) explicit end-marker terminates the span (takes precedence over head duration; keep both paths + the last-beat+handle fallback); (3) beat labels carry item text (the checklist-personal-assistant flow authored content from marker names). Live proof of the target shape: the 10-marker group (start 4491 / 8 labeled beats / END 5701, mixed Purple+Blue) on ReachyMini 'objective', synced+placed by hand-choreographed derivation this session. Amend ADR-0042 grammar section when landing.
result: Grammar v2 landed: marker-sync.ts is color-blind on read (heads by note/customData; explicit END markers close spans with precedence over dragged head duration + end-vs-head-duration lint; every marker inside a delimited span is a beat; orphan lint keys off customData). parseBeatLabel reads item text + roles (- Checked / - Add to list / bare = build-in). Conversational selection via DeriveMarkerSyncOptions.group + buildSyncedMarkerUpdates group param (no more color shim); END joins the Mint receipt as beat -1. 28/28 tests green, svelte-check clean. ADR-0042 amended (+index), brief + resolve-sync skill updated. name: Match number-input steps to schema granularity — no stored value may be :invalid (F-05)
description:
## What
Position Offset Y renders :invalid on load: stored schema-legal 0.115 vs step=0.01 (native validation: 'Please enter a valid value…'). Steps are inconsistent across like fields: offsets 0.01, enter/exit timing 0.001, scale 0.05, rotation 0.5°, others 0.005.

## Why
The control declares the composition wrong when it isn't, and spinner arrows quantize authored values to a coarser grid — an agent-authored preset degrades the moment a GUI author nudges it. Parity betrayal on the core editing path.

## How
Set step to the schema's real granularity per field (0.001 or 'any' for normalized fractions) — one convention for all normalized inputs; audit every number input in the rail against the corpus so no stored value fails checkValidity().
Evidence: a11y tree spinbutton invalid=true; checkValidity() false; step inventory 0.01/0.001/0.05/0.5/0.005.

## Done when
Opening any corpus preset leaves zero :invalid inputs in the rail, and spinner increments match schema granularity per field.
result: Convention: step="any" on every continuous number input (normalized fractions, scale, rotation, z, multipliers, stat from/to) — the corpus audit showed x/y at 4 decimals so 0.001 would still invalidate; Duration seconds 0.5→0.1 (corpus has 1.2/2.8); transition ms 100→10. Also fixed two latent offenders the sweep caught: washi-tape rotation input min was rotationMin(5) vs schema ±25, and source/avatar type=url rejected scheme-less display URLs (now text). Verified: swept all 95 corpus presets in Chrome, selecting every layer and expanding every section — zero :invalid inputs (checkValidity) anywhere.

name: Bound memory for footage-length 4K export
description:
## Goal
Remove the current all-PNG browser buffer and whole-output server/client reads so native 4K/60 source-video exports scale beyond short overlay clips.

## Work
- Measure current peak browser/server memory and throughput on representative 4K/30 and 4K/60 footage before choosing transport. Record the decision in the Source video ADR amendment.
- Replace export-video.ts chunks arrays and aggregate Blob construction with a bounded-memory handoff compatible with the local HTTP stack. Preferred shape: disk-backed browser spooling or a server export session that streams ordered PNG frames into one ffmpeg stdin; choose with measured evidence, not assumption.
- Stream optional WAV exactly once before encoding, validate monotonically ordered frame indexes/count/content type, propagate exact rational framerate and timecode, and apply backpressure so render never outruns encode storage.
- Stream encoded output from disk with @sveltejs/kit/node createReadableStream or an equivalent Web Response stream; avoid readFile and response.blob for large deliverables. Keep GUI download and Playwright CLI download working.
- Make cancel/navigation/server failure kill ffmpeg, close request/readers, dispose decoder samples/textures, remove spool/session/temp files, and never expose partial output. Add session expiry for abandoned jobs if sessions are chosen.
- Preserve existing transparent WebM alpha and ProRes 4444 output for compositions without Source video.

## Verification
Unit/integration tests for frame ordering, backpressure, invalid/missing frames, encoder failure, abort, stale session cleanup, output streaming, and unchanged codecs. Run a creator-scale stress render at native 4K/60 and record peak memory, wall time, frame count, and cleanup evidence.

## Done when
Peak memory is bounded independently of frame count, export starts encoding before the last frame is rendered where the chosen transport permits, and long-job cancellation leaves no ffmpeg process or temp artifact.
result: Replaced all-frame browser PNG accumulation and whole-output reads with a local Node export-session protocol. WAV uploads once to disk; ordered indexed PNG requests validate content type/signature/count and acknowledge only after ffmpeg stdin write-callback backpressure. Completion publishes only successful disk output, streamed with createReadableStream; GUI/Playwright keep native downloads. Abort, encoder/request failure, DELETE, 15-minute expiry, output cancellation, and startup orphan cleanup kill ffmpeg, cancel readers, and remove session files. Preserved exact rational ffmpeg rates, non-drop ProRes timecode, VP9 alpha/opaque formats, and ProRes 4444. Verification: focused 31 tests passed; full Vitest 53 files/228 tests passed; npm run check passed with 0 Svelte diagnostics plus ESLint/discoverability; npm run build passed. Real ffmpeg 8.0.1 probes confirmed VP9 alpha_mode=1, opaque yuv444p, ProRes alpha-bearing 4444 decode, 30000/1001, and 01:00:08:00. A 120-frame 3840x2160/59.94 session completed in 29.081s at 101.6 MiB client peak versus 192.1 MiB for the retired accumulator shape; no ffmpeg/session temp artifacts remained. Playwright CLI live retry was blocked before page creation by the existing shared CDP browser timing out after websocket connection; no browser was terminated or relaunched.

name: Canvas-inspired optical and deformation capability arc
description:
## Goal
Build a clean-room Supers-native family of optical, reveal, deformation, and simulation capabilities inspired by observed CanvasUI behaviors, without importing or porting CanvasUI source, shaders, defaults, assets, or components.

## Why
The current magnify Annotation is visually weak, and the current glass vocabulary is limited to fluted architectural glass. Supers should add physically legible lens/frost/refraction treatments plus deterministic particle, peel, shatter, cloth, fluid, and tiled-deformation motion that works as authored video output rather than interactive website effects.

## Product constraints
- One Preset must render under every Pack and both native orientations.
- Every animation derives from explicit timestamp/frame/progress; no wall-clock or runtime randomness.
- Transparent compositions preserve premultiplied alpha and never paint undeclared backgrounds.
- Final output remains native 3840x2160 or 2160x3840; lower resolutions are allowed only for selected simulation/intermediate fields.
- CanvasUI is behavioral inspiration only. Implement from graphics fundamentals and WICG/WebGPU APIs with independent naming, parameters, shader code, and defaults.
- New Pipelines/domains require a verification Preset and Critic ACCEPT.

## Capability set
- Rebuild focal magnification as a credible optical lens with distortion, edge refraction, controlled chromatic dispersion, haze/frost, and optional Pack-resolved instrument chrome.
- Add non-fluted glass/frost vocabulary: smooth lens glass, frosted/transmission blur, droplets/bubble-style local refraction where compositionally justified.
- Add deterministic particle reveal/dissolve, 3D peel transition, seeded shatter transition, cloth/bend surface deformation, authored fluid/ripple simulation, 2D/3D asset-to-geometry exploration, and tiled deformation.
- Add shared engine seams for dirty DOM generations, pass-local bounds/quality, resource readiness, and seekable stateful GPU simulation where required.

## Done when
Every child epic/task is completed with tests, native horizontal+vertical proving renders, transparent-alpha verification where applicable, GUI schema/editor parity, updated current-truth docs/ADR, and Critic ACCEPT for each new Pipeline family verification Preset.
result: Completed the clean-room optical and deformation capability arc. Shipped rebuilt Magnify plus refractive-lens/frosted-glass optics; render-efficiency and readiness seams; typed particle-dissolve, sheet-peel, and seeded-shatter transitions; a deterministic fixed-step seek/reset/replay runtime; fluid-ripple, cloth-bend, and tiled-deformation Effects; GUI editors, schemas, fixtures, tests, and current-truth ADR/docs. ADR-0047 rejects broad asset-to-geometry import until a bounded Pipeline needs it. Independent Critics ACCEPTed the optical showcase and all six new transition/material/deformation fixtures at native horizontal and vertical. Final verification passed: git diff --check, npm run check, verify-presets, test:structural, build, test:browser, and npm test (75 files, 342 tests). No commit was created because none was requested.

name: Make Factory observability automatic and lifecycle-wide
description:
## Goal
Make Sentry observability an automatic, non-gating part of every Supers Planning and Delivery Factory lifecycle so we can measure effectiveness, profile stage performance, and diagnose Factory failures.

## Requirements

## Done when
A normal terminal lifecycle path automatically writes a Sentry receipt and visible Sentry data for both factories; failure/outcome and stage profiling dimensions are queryable; duplicate execution does not double count; Sentry failure cannot change Factory outcome; tests, model validation, workflow validation, project checks, and a live end-to-end verification pass.
result: Built lifecycle-native Sentry observability for both Supers Factories. Delivery now routes done and aborted through observer stages; Planning routes done, rejected, parked, failed-apply, failed-audit, and aborted. Observer workflows terminalize first, persist canonical summaries, emit best-effort bounded metrics and reconstructed run/stage traces, and verify exact local receipt coverage. Sentry failure cannot change terminal Factory status, while missing or degraded telemetry fails the observer workflow visibly. Added idempotent replay, old-receipt compatibility, package/docs/changelogs, materialized models/workflows, extensive tests, and live Sentry proof.

name: Half-res 4K perf for the depth stage
description: The stage renders full-res 4K through scene→mip-pyramid→DOF; perf headroom was flagged at POC. Render the scene half-res + upsample where quality holds (text-critical pieces stay on the flat ADR-0027 path anyway). Measure before/after frame times at 3840×2160 + 2160×3840.
result: Half-res 4K DOF built + measured. The 96-tap gather now renders into a half-res target (sampling the unchanged FULL-res scene mip pyramid — UV space is resolution-independent, so the blur itself loses nothing) and a new full-res compose pass re-injects the sharp scene where the image is in focus. Blend mask = max(center CoC, gather's bleed-reach alpha): the gather records the max tap CoC that actually reached each pixel, so a defocused foreground still bleeds smoothly over an in-focus plane (no hard cheap-DOF edge). Film grade + vignette moved from the gather to the compose so sharp and blurred regions wear one grade. aperture≈0 skips pyramid+gather entirely (compose is a pure passthrough+grade). Measured with new scripts/cdp-measure-fps.mjs (5s playback window, native 4K backing): horizontal 3840x2160 32.0 → 47.2 fps; vertical 2160x3840 25.8 → 44.8 fps. Quality verified at native 4K: in-focus text tack-sharp (full-res path), defocused card smooth with no upsample artifacts, blurred-edge-over-sharp-overlay transition clean, aperture-0 pullquote-on-photo unchanged, vertical reflow clean. Determinism 194/8.28M px (0.0023%, max delta 2) — the pre-existing mip-race residual, within bar. svelte-check 0 errors. ADR-0028 + engine-architecture.md updated with measured numbers.

name: Source video underlay and full-rate export
description:
## Goal
Make a creator video a first-class composition input rendered beneath every Supers Layer in preview and baked export, preserving exact transport frame rate and native 3840x2160 or 2160x3840 output. This is the foundation for a later automatic editor that removes silence and places overlays.

## V1 product contract
- Canonical term: Source video. It is composition input beneath the five Layers, not a Surface, Substrate, preview backdrop, or Effect.
- One content-addressed local source asset, one continuous source range, and one composition-wide trim offset. The composition starts at source offset and requires enough source duration to cover transport.durationSeconds.
- Centered cover framing at native target size in both orientations. Decode at encoded source resolution; never render through a reduced composition intermediate.
- transport remains authoritative for duration, exact rational FPS, orientation, and output format. At every output timestamp select the source sample presented at or before the mapped source timestamp; VFR and B-frame media must not drift.
- Source audio is included by default, may be muted or gain-adjusted, and mixes deterministically with existing Supers cues into the current 48 kHz stereo export track.
- Existing Supers Effects process the transparent animation result only. The source is composited in the final present pass so Pack chrome and post-process Effects never silently grade creator footage.
- Source video makes output opaque. V1 rejects simultaneous backgroundFill, dimensional stage, and transition Presets rather than hiding footage or freezing it in transition snapshots.

## Out of scope
Silence detection, cut generation, multiple clips, timeline edit lists, speed changes, loops/holds, source-footage color grading, depth-stage video planes, and live dual-tree video transitions.

## Done when
A GUI- or agent-authored User composition can attach local MP4/MOV/WebM footage, scrub it in sync under animation, export WebM and ProRes with retained source audio plus cues, and pass decoded-output verification at horizontal and vertical native sizes at 30, 30000/1001, 60, and 60000/1001 rates. Long footage export has bounded browser/server memory, cancellation cleans decoder/ffmpeg/temp resources, and current truth is documented.
result: Source video v1 is complete. GUI and agent workflows ingest immutable MP4/MOV/WebM assets, preserve the shared Preset model, scrub and play through the explicit Timeline decoder, composite native creator pixels beneath all five Layers after Supers Effects, retain/mix Source audio with cues, and export through bounded local ffmpeg sessions with streamed output and full cancellation/expiry cleanup. All nine child tasks passed. Decoded matrix: 8 native outputs across 3840x2160/2160x3840, 30/30000-1001/60/60000-1001, opaque VP9 WebM/ProRes 4444, Source audio on/off/cue mixes, plus transparent and opaque controls. Preview-to-ProRes comparisons all passed (max MAE 0.01822). Final gates: 53 test files/229 tests, 18 structural tests plus 3 structural scripts, all Presets, npm run check, production build, CLI single/batch, browser health with 672 responses and zero console/network errors, cancellation and memory evidence. ADR-0043 and current-truth docs are updated. Silence cutting remains a separate approval-gated future arc.

name: SurfaceInspector — structural fix + thoughtful design (ADR-0034 §9)
description:
The SurfaceInspector is the most broken inspector and was treated as an afterthought — it must not be. This is a major interface; every inch needs thoughtful design.

STRUCTURAL BUGS to fix:
- It uses class .row for every content/appearance field. .row IS defined in Graffiti (index.css ~L1947) but only gets its real layout power inside <form>/<fieldset> (':is(form,fieldset) .row > label' etc). The SurfaceInspector markup is plain divs/labels, so the fields get only the bare base rule and look unstyled. Either wrap the field groups so the Graffiti form .row styling applies, OR move to the same section/field system the other inspectors use (ww2wpmoz). Keep .row only if it actually earns its styling — otherwise drop it. Decide deliberately, don't leave it half-applied.
- .anim-entry uses 'border: var(--border-1); border-radius' — a bordered CARD, which ADR-0034 §9 explicitly forbids (no boxes-within-boxes). Replace with the spacing + 1px-divider + inline-label pattern.
- The section divider is on .section__header, opposite of RootInspector/OverlayInspector. Unify with the shared §9 system.

DESIGN: align with the inspector design language from ww2wpmoz (do that first or in tandem). Content fields (type picker, kicker/title/source/body, AnnotationTextEditor, appearance colors, Text Motion) need consistent label-column alignment, intentional spacing, and a clear reading order. NO progressive disclosure. Graffiti tokens. Apply design-engineering + typography + ux-interface-design + graffiti-best-practices.

DONE: no undefined/half-applied classes; no bordered cards; consistent with the §9 section system; every field intentionally laid out. Chrome screenshot proof of the SurfaceInspector on a paper/web-document preset required before close.
result:
SurfaceInspector redesigned onto the shared §9 system (ADR-0034 §9). Verified in Chrome (localhost:7263, research-paper-attention paper preset). Scott confirmed.

FILE: src/lib/platform/SurfaceInspector.svelte.

FIXES: (1) converted every field from bare Graffiti .row / plain divs to InspectorSection + Field, so SURFACE/APPEARANCE/TEXT MOTION use the same §9 dividers + label-aligned dense fields as the other inspectors. (2) Killed the .anim-entry bordered CARD (border + border-radius, a §9 boxes-within-boxes violation) -> hairline sub-divider (border-block-start only; verified border-radius 0, borderWidth 1px 0 0). (3) Fixed the divider placement — was border-block-end on .section__header (opposite the other inspectors); now the §9 top-divider via InspectorSection. (4) Body (tall AnnotationTextEditor + mark toolbar) gets a stacked full-width treatment (label above) instead of being forced into the label-left grid. (5) remove/clear buttons -> borderless red × consistent with the others.

VERIFIED: SURFACE (Type/Title/Source/Author + Body editor), APPEARANCE (Font/Paper/Ink), TEXT MOTION (per-slot + Effect pickers + a hairline-separated anim entry with Effect/Enter/Speed/Hold/Gap). Added+removed a Title text-anim to confirm the anim-entry renders as a hairline (not a card). svelte-check clean (2 pre-existing engine-schema errors only). name: Mix Source video audio with Supers cues
description:
## Goal
Retain the creator footage audio by default and mix it frame-deterministically with existing motion/manual cues in preview and exported media.

## Work
- Decode the selected source range through Mediabunny AudioSampleSink. Convert channel layouts and sample rates into the existing deterministic 48 kHz stereo mix with explicit sample-index placement; do not schedule export audio through wall-clock Web Audio playback.
- Apply sourceVideo.includeAudio and bounded gain, then mix existing automatic/manual cues. Source audio is footage audio, not a bed; update bed/full-frame validation without conflating those concepts.
- Define clipping policy, channel downmix, resampling, leading timestamps, trim boundaries, missing-audio behavior, and output duration at the exact export frame count. Keep soundless sources free of an empty audio stream unless Supers cues exist.
- Extend AudioPreview so Timeline play/loop starts the same trimmed source mix and cues at current explicit timeline time; scrub remains silent under current product policy.
- Ensure Separate WAV downloads the final source-plus-cue mix and WebM/ProRes mux the same WAV.

## Tests
Fixtures with stereo 48 kHz, mono 44.1 kHz, multichannel, delayed audio start, no audio track, source gain/mute, cue overlap, fractional frame-rate duration, and source shorter than composition. Assert sample placement, duration, channels, peak policy, no silent stream, and cancellation cleanup.

## Done when
Preview playback and decoded WebM/ProRes exports preserve lip-sync across the full clip and the mixed cue lands on the same composition frame as before Source video support.
result: Implemented Mediabunny AudioSampleSink Source audio decode with video-relative PTS, trim offset, delayed starts, deterministic 48 kHz stereo resampling/downmix, bounded gain/mute, missing-track silence, exact rational-frame output length, AbortSignal disposal, cue summing, one peak policy, and shared final mix for WebM/ProRes/Separate WAV. AudioPreview now plays that same final source-plus-cue mix from the explicit Timeline playhead, restarts on loops, remains silent on scrub, and cancels stale decode/playback on pause. Verified 34 focused tests, full npm run check, and real sanctioned-Chrome AAC decode: 240000 samples at 48 kHz, nonzero peak, three frame timestamps through the clip.

name: Implement deterministic Source video decoder
description:
## Goal
Resolve every explicit composition timestamp to the correct decoded source presentation sample with one lifecycle shared by preview and export.

## Work
- Build a concept-named SourceVideoDecoder around Mediabunny Input plus a range-backed CustomSource, VideoSampleSink, and track metadata. Keep Mediabunny at the trust boundary and expose strict project types.
- Map composition timestamp to sourceOffsetSeconds + timestamp. VideoSampleSink.getSample semantics must select the last presentation sample at or before that time; export should use a sequential samples-at-timestamps path when faster, while random preview seeks remain exact.
- Handle VFR, B-frames, 23.976/29.97/59.94 transport timestamps, source FPS lower/higher than output, rotation, visible rect, pixel aspect ratio, color metadata, first-frame offset, and end coverage.
- Close every VideoSample/VideoFrame immediately after GPU upload, abort stale async seeks, prevent an old seek from painting over a newer playhead, and dispose input/sinks/resources on source replacement and Workspace teardown.
- Introduce a source-video frame preparation seam that CompositionExportController awaits before renderCompositionFrameTo; never rely on HTMLVideoElement.currentTime, requestVideoFrameCallback, wall-clock playback, or HTML-in-Canvas capture.

## Tests
Pure timestamp mapping tests plus decoder integration fixtures generated with ffmpeg: CFR frame-number slate, NTSC rational cadence, VFR durations, B-frame GOP, rotated portrait, non-square pixels, short source, no-video track, and unsupported codec. Assert chosen sample PTS for first/middle/last and repeated backward/forward seeks.

## Done when
The same requested timestamp deterministically produces the same source sample in random preview seeks and serial export, with no leaked samples or stale-seek races.
result: Implemented SourceVideoDecoder over Mediabunny UrlSource and VideoSampleSink with 64 MiB range cache, browser codec gating, exact first-PTS plus media-relative offset mapping, source coverage validation, random getSample selection, optimized samplesAtTimestamps export iteration, closable frame ownership, stale seek suppression, abort handling, and deterministic disposal. Added pure timing utilities and a CDP integration probe. Verification: 5 focused tests passed for NTSC timestamp math, coverage, stale seek closure, export iteration, and disposal; svelte-check 0 errors/warnings; targeted ESLint and git diff --check passed. Live sanctioned CDP Chrome decoded a generated H.264/AAC 30000/1001 source with B-frames over range requests: exact PTS at frames 0, 1, and 30, and last-sample-at-or-before behavior at 2.5s; metadata reported 29.97002997 fps and 640x360. Generated source/store files were removed.

name: Add the deterministic discoverability gate
description:
## Goal
Turn objective searchability conventions into a required check without duplicating TypeScript or ESLint guarantees.

## Scope

Enforce no forwarding/wildcard re-exports, configured prohibited generic exported names, canonical terminology aliases, searchable error prefixes where mechanically safe, and source/test naming consistency where a paired test exists. Wire it into npm run check.

## Requirements
Do not duplicate no-explicit-any or strict TypeScript checks already provided by ESLint/TypeScript. Account for framework-required exports and concept-qualified index.ts/types.ts paths. Use a reviewed allowlist for legitimate exceptions; avoid subjective file-size or word-count linting.

## Done when
The gate catches seeded violations, passes the cleaned repository, is exercised by focused tests, and npm run check runs it successfully.
result: Added scripts/check-discoverability.mjs, a deterministic TypeScript-compiler-API audit over active TypeScript/JavaScript and extracted Svelte script blocks. Wired npm run check:discoverability after svelte-check and ESLint in npm run check; structural verification now also runs the focused node:test suite. Enforced: production-source wildcard/export-from and imported-symbol forwarding exports; exact generic export denylist only under src/lib; exact retired canonical identifiers only under src/lib; empty/interpolation-first Error, TypeError, and RangeError messages where the AST can prove the prefix unsafe; paired test names when a same-basename source exists or exactly one relative/ primary source resolves. Framework route exports and concept-qualified index.ts/types.ts remain valid. Reviewed exceptions are exact: textAnimationGsapInstance forwarding in manager.svelte.ts, and the operation interpolation in user-composition-store.ts whose callers supply fixed searchable prefixes. Added valid and violating fixtures; 4 focused tests prove all five rules, both forwarding forms, actionable file/line/rule/remediation output, framework/index/types conventions, CLI failure, and the current repository. Verification: direct checker passed 369 source files; focused tests 4/4; npm run check passed with 0 Svelte diagnostics and clean ESLint; npm test passed 27 files/118 tests; npm run test:structural passed 4 discoverability tests plus 3 existing scripts; npm run verify-presets passed all Presets, 35 fixtures, Pack contracts, and Identity registry; npm run build passed with only the existing large-chunk advisory; git diff --check passed. One concurrent npm test/build sweep caused the existing dynamic-import hook to exceed 10 seconds; npm test passed in isolation immediately afterward. name: Resolve optical Critic round-two findings
description:
## Goal
Resolve the post-R2 Critic findings preventing optical-lens-showcase ACCEPT.

## Pipeline findings
- Frosted-glass sparse 17-tap transmission produces discrete repeated glyph ghosts instead of continuous rough scattering.
- Magnify hardcodes visible iris entry/exit to 10% of Mark progress, yielding ~66 ms transitions and violating Q15/G6 for legal Mark durations.
- Paper Surface vertical reflow places readable content at x=29 and source label near y=3494, outside title/platform safe areas.

## Preset findings
- Focal frame has four perceptual saturated hue clusters; Q4 allows at most three.
- Frost growth spans 720 ms; G6 entry window is 250-400 ms.
- Surface exit is 33.3% shorter than entry; G6 requires 20-30%.

## Requirements
Fix defects in owning Pipeline/default code, not by hiding them in the Preset. Tune only findings classified preset-choice. Preserve deterministic native horizontal/vertical rendering, alpha-safe compositing, and Pack neutrality.

## Done when
Focused tests, npm run check, npm run verify-presets, npm run build, native captures/probes, and a fresh isolated Critic all pass with zero pipeline-bug/default-too-permissive findings.
result: Resolved round-two frost ghosting, Magnify timing, vertical safe-area reflow, hue count, frost growth, and Surface exit findings. Frost now uses a 169-tap isotropic gaussian kernel and all timing/safety gates pass.

name: Verify native full-rate Source video export
description:
## Goal
Prove decoded deliverables, not just preview pixels, preserve source timing, overlay compositing, audio sync, exact rate, native dimensions, and old transparent behavior.

## Work
- Generate deterministic source fixtures with visible frame number/time quadrants and frame-aligned audio clicks. Include horizontal, rotated portrait, CFR, VFR, B-frame, and NTSC cadence inputs.
- Extend probe-export-decode.ts or add a concept-focused probe that ffprobes width, height, r_frame_rate/avg_frame_rate, decoded frame count, duration, pixel format, audio streams/sample rate/channels, and sampled source-frame identity.
- At frame 0/middle/last and crop boundaries compare preview capture to decoded ProRes output within the documented codec tolerance. Assert overlays animate, premultiplied edges are clean, source pixels outside animation are unchanged by Effects, and no frame repeats/drops beyond mathematically required source-to-output cadence.
- Required matrix: horizontal 3840x2160 and vertical 2160x3840; 30, 30000/1001, 60, and 60000/1001; WebM opaque and ProRes 4444; source audio on/off plus cue mix. Include one existing transparent-overlay control export and one existing opaque bumper control.
- Run npm test, npm run test:structural, npm run check, npm run verify-presets, npm run build, browser console/network checks on localhost:7263 after confirming the port, and CLI render/batch smoke.
- Update docs/engine-architecture.md, docs/preset-format.md, docs/roadmap.md, docs/user-composition-workflows.md, Sentry flow docs, and ADR status to current truth.

## Done when
All matrix outputs pass machine assertions, no source/animation A/V drift is measurable at the last frame, no regression appears in transparent exports, memory/cancellation evidence is recorded in the Dex result, and the epic is ready for the human check-in before any silence-cutting arc starts.
result: Machine verification completed 2026-07-27. Added deterministic CFR/VFR/B-frame/NTSC/rotated Source fixtures, public-CLI matrix preparation/rendering, preview capture, decoded-output assertions, CDP page health, and export-session cancellation probes. All 8 native outputs passed: 3840x2160 and 2160x3840; 30, 30000/1001, 60, and 60000/1001; opaque VP9 WebM and ProRes 4444; Source audio on/off, cue-only, and Source+cue mix. Decoded frame identities matched the presentation-sample rule with only mathematically required repeats; dimensions, frame counts, crop boundaries, overlay motion, unchanged Source pixels outside Effects, alpha, and codec/profile assertions passed. All 12 frame-0/middle/last ProRes preview comparisons passed (maximum MAE 0.01822 under the documented 0.035 tolerance). Audio was exact whole-frame 48 kHz stereo (9600 or 9610 samples); Source/cue peaks had zero accumulated drift and at most one-sample endpoint rounding. Existing controls passed: lower-third transparent WebM 150 frames with partial alpha edges and bounded VP9 hidden-color reconstruction; type-hero opaque WebM 180 frames at alpha 255. Browser health at localhost:7263 passed at 3840x2160 with CanvasDrawElement/timeline/export seams, 673 responses, zero console errors, and zero network errors. Three live FFmpeg cancellation cycles passed: every encoder exited, every private session directory was removed, no resources remained, and warmed server RSS differed by 16 KiB across the final two cycles. Public CLI single render and eight-job batch smoke passed. Gates passed: npm test (53 files/229 tests), test:structural, verify-presets, check (0 diagnostics plus lint/discoverability), build, supers-cli focused tests (7), and script ESLint. Documented transport caveats: WebM's 1 ms timebase quantizes NTSC PTS within 0.000484 s and may not report the literal rational through ffprobe; ProRes reports exact rationals. FFmpeg 8 may log a nonfatal Opus packet-header warning while decoding the exact expected PCM samples. ProRes 4444 currently decodes as yuva444p12le from the encoder's yuva444p10le request. Updated ADR-0043/ADR index/roadmap to machine-verified and preserved the mandatory human check-in before silence cutting.

name: Fix canvas drag — overlay position update and persist — task 79k0lp29 was marked done but coordinate math was broken throughout. The drag currently does not correctly reposition overlays on canvas in a way that persists. Done: drag an overlay on canvas → position.offset updates live in the inspector; value survives a route reload (persisted via userStore).
description:
Canvas drag — overlay position update + persist (ADR-0034 §1). Prior task 79k0lp29 marked done but the coordinate math was broken throughout — drag does not correctly reposition overlays on canvas in a way that persists.

The hard part is coordinate mapping: screen px → scaled-canvas px → 4K composition space → schema offset (0..1). The canvas is a WebGPU target with a DOM editing overlay (CanvasEditingOverlay.svelte) on top of a fit-to-window scaled canvas; the overlay's own root can collapse to 0x0 so coords must be projected against the frame-sized .composition ancestor (see memory: overlay-root-collapses-project-against-composition). Drag writes overlay.position.offset {x,y}.

DONE: drag an overlay on canvas → position.offset updates LIVE in the OverlayInspector number fields; the dragged value survives a route reload (persisted via userStore autosave/fork). Verify with Chrome at localhost:7263: drag, read inspector value, reload, confirm it held. Screenshot proof required.
result:
Canvas drag fixed + completed end-to-end. Verified in Chrome (localhost:7263) across lower-third (bottom-left), watermark (top-right + center-convert), shader-fill (normalized-rect).

FILES: src/lib/platform/CanvasEditingOverlay.svelte, src/lib/platform/Workspace.svelte.

CORE FIX (CanvasEditingOverlay drag math): offset is an INSET from the anchor edge, so the old 'origin + delta' inverted right/bottom anchors. Now anchor-aware signed deltas (left:+dx, right:-dx, top:+dy, bottom:-dy); normalized-rect drags rect.x/y; center converts to free top-left placement on first real move (seeded from measured position so it doesn't jump). Sub-pixel jitter threshold so a click doesn't reanchor/drag.

TWO REACTIVITY GAPS FIXED: (1) Workspace composition-sync $effect now tracks overlay.position.* — previously a drag OR an inspector offset edit didn't repaint the canvas live; (2) CanvasEditingOverlay overlayRelRect now subscribes to position so the selection/hit box re-measures and tracks the overlay (was sticking to the original spot).

UX ADDITIONS from Scott review: (a) editor opens on a SETTLED frame (SETTLED_PREVIEW_FRACTION=0.5) so overlays are visible on load instead of an empty t=0 canvas — this was why drag 'didn't seem to work'; (b) draggable affordance — overlays show grab/grabbing cursor + a hover ring (reveal-on-hover, no permanent chrome); surface shows default cursor + nothing, signalling base-layer-not-draggable.

VERIFIED: all 4 edge directions correct (measured offset deltas = exact px/canvas fractions); center-convert (no jump, anchor center->top-left, hit center matches drag target); shader-fill rect (left 30%->41.8%, top 35%->47.6%, hit tracks); persistence — dragged offset survives route reload (works because the user-composition persistence bug jsgbq9kf was fixed). All 8 overlay types draggable. svelte-check clean (only 2 pre-existing engine-schema.ts errors). Console clean.

SCOPE NOTE: surfaces (paper/newspaper/web-document/imessage) are intentionally NOT draggable — SurfaceSchema has no position field; they are the base layer (ADR-0034 §1 spatial-subset boundary). Scott confirmed this is correct. Rotation captured as a separate new task.

name: Drive concurrent Factory epics through isolated worktrees
description: Use the existing @swamp/software-factory concurrency model and the Pi Factory driver; do not add or extend a Git model. One Factory instance may track many root-epic work items concurrently. The parent driver selects at most one ready Dex leaf per root epic, launches each independent epic through Pi with worktree:true, and lets runner capacity bound concurrency dynamically. Factory state, approvals, and evidence remain in the central Swamp repository while implementation happens in the isolated checkout. The parent consumes Pi worktree handoffs and serializes integration, verifying the recorded source revision, tree fingerprint, target revision, and changed paths before each integration. Dependency-related epics must wait; overlapping changes that cannot integrate cleanly return to rework rather than mutating another lane. Acceptance: prove at least two unrelated epics can run concurrently without sharing a checkout; prove one active leaf per root; prove no fixed lane cap; prove integrations are one-at-a-time and stale handoffs are rejected; record all handoff and integration evidence through @swamp/software-factory. No custom @swamp/git extension or shell-wrapped Git integration.

name: Fix unified clip bar — ADR-0034 §2a specifies one continuous bar per overlay with 5 drag handles (left outer trim, left inner fade, body move, right inner fade, right outer trim) and enter-ramp/solid/exit-ramp visual zones. description:
Unified clip bar — DaVinci single-bar-per-layer model (ADR-0034 §2a). NOT close to done: the prior agent left the OLD model in place. Today a layer's timeline row still renders as a separate enter block + connector + separate exit block with a gap between them (TimelineOutline.svelte track-connector + two track-transition spans). The overlay branch in Workspace.buildTracks() computes enterZone/exitZone but the rendering + drag still behaves as the old two-block model and other track types (surface, mark, text-anim, imessage, instance-stack/counter/spin/cursor sub-tracks) are entirely two-block/separate-clip.

TARGET (how it works in DaVinci Resolve / Premiere): ONE continuous bar per layer item. In/out are HANDLES ON THE SAME BAR, not separate clips. Five drag zones per ADR-0034 §2a:
- left outer edge → trim clip start (enter.start)
- left inner fade handle → enter.duration (enter/solid boundary)
- body → move whole clip (shift enter.start + exit.start together)
- right inner fade handle → exit.duration (solid/exit boundary)
- right outer edge → trim clip end (exit.start + exit.duration)
Visual zones: enter ramp (gradient) | solid | exit ramp (gradient), integrated into the single bar fill. No enter → starts solid w/ right ramp only. No exit → ends solid. Text-anim rows = enter-only single bar. Audio-cue rows = point markers.

DONE: every layer renders as ONE bar (verified for overlay, surface, mark, text-anim — not just overlays); all 5 handles drag and write the correct schema fields; ramp gradients visible at the bar ends; NO connector/gap/two-block rendering remains anywhere. Chrome screenshot proof of a multi-layer composition required before close.

Apply css-motion-systems + design-engineering for the bar styling and handle affordances.

Every Layer (surface, mark, overlay, text-anim, iMessage) renders as ONE continuous bar with 5 drag handles; two-block connector model + dead TimelineTrackView/TimelineScrubber removed. Bar represents PERCEIVED presence: handles sit where each ease's motion actually lands (ease tail collapsed into the underlying duration), verified against the real rendered transform — playhead reaching a handle == motion finishing, within ~2% for back.out (settled) and power3.out (smooth). New utils: timeline-clip.ts (pure geometry + 5-handle drag, unit-tested), ease-landing.ts (per-ease landing from gsap/cubic-bezier/steps). During dwell from===to so velocity/trail collapse; sin envelope eases trail in/out of glides (removed magic dwellThreshold). buildTracks surfaces one draggable dwell clip per waypoint (width=dwellMs, start=arrival; drag writes back dwellMs/travelMs). name: Implement the typed Dex plan applier
description:
## Scope
Create @club_aqua_back_deck/dex-plan-applier as a Swamp model extension with one fan-out apply-plan method. Accept a fully typed, already human-approved plan containing an optional epic, tasks, parent references, priorities, blocker edges, and descriptions. Search/validate referenced existing tasks, create the hierarchy deterministically, preserve exact priorities and descriptions, and return a stable client-reference-to-Dex-id mapping plus versioned receipts.

## Constraints
Use official Dex CLI/MCP interfaces with structured arguments; never read or write .dex/tasks.jsonl directly. Acquire one model invocation lock and perform the graph mutation serially inside it instead of N competing Swamp calls. Fail closed before mutation on duplicate client references, cycles, missing references, invalid hierarchy depth, or ambiguous existing-task matches. Make retry/idempotency semantics explicit so a partial failure cannot duplicate an epic or task. Do not decide planning content, mutate documentation, or bypass the planning Factory human approval gate.

name: Design the lifecycle observability contract
description: Define automatic terminal routing, outcome mapping, profiling signals, receipt coverage, and non-gating failure semantics for Planning and Delivery.
result:
Defined the lifecycle observability contract:
- Observability is a required lifecycle stage before every terminal state, not a manual post-run command.
- Each outcome-specific observability stage runs one factory-specific workflow that first advances to the real terminal state, then invokes summary and the Sentry emitter as allowFailure steps. Sentry availability cannot alter the terminal outcome.
- Delivery covers done and aborted. Planning covers done, rejected, parked, failed-apply, failed-audit, and aborted; custom failure terminals retain their exact failedStage while the canonical broad outcome remains parked.
- The emitter remains the single network boundary and expands bounded metrics for stage visits/dispatches/time-to-gate, human touches, and failed terminal stage so Sentry supports profiling and diagnosis as well as completion counts.
- Both reusable profile compilers gain optional terminal-observer workflow configuration so materialization cannot erase the wiring and consumers without an observer remain backward compatible.
- A Swamp-native coverage method will compare every terminal state/journal key against emitter receipts. Missing coverage is explicit local data and a failing audit gate, not silent dashboard absence.
- Normal lifecycle verification must prove automatic receipt creation; direct invocation of the telemetry workflow is not acceptable evidence.
Architecture basis: Swamp workflows orchestrate multiple model methods; the emitter model owns the external Sentry action; reports remain deterministic analysis only, consistent with the Swamp architecture guide and docs/project-control-plane.md.
